Moses designated three cities on the eastern bank of the Jordan, where the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh settled: one in the south where the tribe of Reuben is, which is Bezer; the second in the middle where the tribe of Gad is, which is Ramoth in Gilead; and the third in the north within the borders of half the tribe of Manasseh, which is Golan.

God appointed these cities so that anyone who killed a person unintentionally might flee to them. Since the custom of taking vengeance was common in Bedouin societies, including Israel, it was necessary to set aside these cities for this purpose.
As we shall see later, three other cities were designated on the western bank to serve the same purpose for the tribes that would settle there.
With this the first sermon of Moses the prophet ends, which began at the beginning of this book, and the second sermon begins at the next verse.

If a person is hard in his feelings because of his selfishness, so that he takes vengeance on the one who killed one of his loved ones, yet God's mercy preserves even sinners, especially those who sin unintentionally as long as they repent, just as He appointed the cities of refuge for one who falls into accidental killing. Therefore trust in God's mercies whatever your sins, for He loves you and wants your salvation.
The law: the Law, which includes the divine commands and ordinances that Moses received from God on the mountain.
The testimonies: God's commandments and judgments, which bear witness to the existence of God and bear witness against the people so that they hold fast to them and do not transgress them.

This is the introduction to the second sermon of Moses, in which he repeats the divine commandments and laws that he had mentioned before in (Ex 20-23); he repeats them here because the fathers who heard them in the Book of Exodus have died, and these are their sons who will enter the Promised Land. Therefore this book was called Deuteronomy, that is, the repetition and confirmation of the Law, and the sermon will extend from here to (ch. 26:19).
Beyond the Jordan: the eastern bank of the Jordan.
Peor: the temple of the god Peor, the god of the Moabites.
The valley: the plains.
The land of Sihon: it lies east of the Jordan (Num 21:25-27; ch. 2:24).
Heshbon: the capital of the Amorites, whose king was Sihon.
The land of Og: it lies east of the Jordan River (ch. 3:1). Aroer: a Moabite city (ch. 2:36). The valley of Arnon): ch. 2:24.(The Arabah: the region between the Dead Sea and the Red Sea.

Mount Sion: the same as Mount Hermon (ch. 3:8). The sea of the plain: the Dead Sea (map 15). Moses makes clear the place where he delivered this second sermon of his (map 15), and also makes clear the people's possession of the land which Sihon had held, and also the land which Og king of Bashan had held, both lands being on the eastern bank of the Jordan. Then he defined geographically the boundaries of those lands from the city of Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of Arnon, in the south, to Mount Hermon in the north, that is, the whole region through which the Jordan River, the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea run, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah, on the eastern side of the river.

God repeats His voice to us more than once and in more than one way so that we do not forget His commandments, out of His concern for our salvation. May we give heed to His voice and hasten to carry out His commandments.
The Ten Commandments

entries.section: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

paragraphs.text: Learn them: understand them.
Keep: take care and be exact, because of the gravity of the words.
The second sermon begins with Moses' call to the people to give heed to hearing the Ten Commandments, which are God's statutes and His basic judgments for the people's conduct.

Then he asks them to take them in and understand their meanings deeply so that they may enjoy their power. The third thing Moses asked is that they do these commandments, so that they become life in them.

Turn everything you read in the Bible into practical application in your life, for approving and understanding the divine word is not enough, and may you take one verse each day, memorize it, repeat it and meditate on its meanings, so that this helps you apply it throughout the day.

entries.section: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

paragraphs.text: Moses reminds them of the covenant which God made with their fathers at Mount Horeb, when He appeared to them in a great fire and mist on the mountain and gave them the commandments and the Law by the hand of Moses. When Moses came down from the mountain, he built an altar and twelve pillars as a confirmation of the participation of all the tribes in the covenant. He wrote the commandments and the Law in a book and sacrificed sacrifices and sprinkled the blood on the altar and on the people, confirming the covenant with blood, which is a type of the blood of Christ the Redeemer in the New Testament, by which we obtain salvation (Ex 24:6-8).

entries.section: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

paragraphs.text: God made the covenant with the fathers who disobeyed Him by refusing to enter the Promised Land out of fear of those who lived in it, so He commanded that they be deprived of entering it, and they wandered in the wilderness until all the adult men died. Therefore the sons who are hearing Moses now might think that the covenant is not with them, so Moses affirms here that the covenant is with them and not with their fathers; this is God's intention, because God knows that the fathers will refuse to obey Him. He meant the sons who were children at that time or would be born afterwards, because they are the ones who will obey Him, so He will bring them into the land of Canaan. And with them, of course, were Caleb and Joshua.

entries.section: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

paragraphs.text: To confirm the covenant, Moses declares that it was with God Himself and not by means of an angel or any mediator. What is meant by their seeing God face to face is seeing the fire on the mountain and hearing His voice, and this calls for holding fast to the covenant, the commandments and the Law, because they are from God directly.

entries.section: (1) The call to the people to hear the commandments

paragraphs.text: Moses reminds them that he was a witness of God's presence and His speaking with the people, indeed he was a mediator between them and God, because they feared the sight of the mountain and the fire on it, so he drew near to the mountain and went up alone upon it and heard the commandments and the Law, and then told them to the people. After that Moses began to repeat the commandments to them, and therefore at the end of the verse it is written, "saying."

And just as Moses was a mediator between the people and God, so too Christ is the Mediator of the New Testament, who redeemed us by His blood and through whom we have access before the Father (Heb 8:6, Heb 12:24,.)
Before Me: that is, beside Me.

The first commandment is God's making Himself known to His people, and He makes the people know well that they did not come out of bondage in Egypt by their own strength, but that there was a lofty power able to bring them out, and this power is the power of Almighty God, and that He does not accept that His people worship other gods alongside their worship of Him, but He alone must be the God who is worshipped, without partner or equal.
The second commandment:

In the second commandment the Lord forbids them to carve images for the purpose of worship resembling any of the forms found in heaven, like the planets, stars and moons, or found on the surface of the earth, like men and beasts, or found in the seas, like fish.

Bowing down is a bodily expression of submission and obedience from the one who bows to the one bowed to, and since God is the only Being to whom we owe this, He never allows bowing down to any other; even if there is no bowing down but standing in a spirit of reverence and submission, that is, worship, this too is not permitted to any but the one God. Hence the two expressions "thou shalt not bow down thyself to them" and "nor serve them" were necessary.

The Lord your God is a jealous God: in many places of the Bible the Lord likens His relationship with His people (His Church) to the relationship of a bridegroom with his bride or a husband with his wife.

Just as a bridegroom loves his bride and gives her every care and tenderness, he expects her to return love for love and tenderness with awe and submission. And a husband cannot bear that another person share in the love of his wife. So too the Lord is a jealous God who does not allow His beloved, that is, His people, to divide their love and worship, some of it for the true God and some for other gods, which would mean a loyalty to God that is not complete.

Here is a discussion of blessing and curse: the blessing which God bestows on those who love Him and keep His commandments, for love of God appears in holding fast to His commandments and doing them; and the curse that befalls those who do not love Him and hate Him in themselves, and its effects are reflected on their children after them. For the consequences of sin extend their effects to the following generations, as in the scattering of the Jewish people as a punishment for their rejection of Christ, whose effect extended to generations after the generation that rejected Christ.
The third commandment:

A warning against the misuse of the name of God in any form, such as swearing by it falsely or in unseemly matters. A person must show complete reverence and utter respect for the name of the Lord, and mention it only with all awe and respect and only when there is real necessity. If a person transgresses this commandment, God punishes him.

This commandment keeps them away from using the names of the pagan gods, so that they swear only by the name of God, but with all esteem and respect. In Christianity, however, after spiritual maturity and steadfastness in the faith, swearing is not permitted, because the name of God is too high to be used in material dealings.
The fourth commandment:
Sabbath: a Hebrew word meaning "rest."
To sanctify it: to set it apart.
He commanded that the Sabbath day be set apart for the Lord, for it is a day for worship and rest from the usual daily works.
Thy gates: your cities.
Stranger: a guest or visitor.

A person works six days of the week to provide for his material needs, but he needs to set apart a day of rest from work so that he may be free for worship. And God, who knows man's needs, commanded that man, beast and guest rest in all the cities of Israel, as well as the manservants and maidservants, reminding the people that they too were slaves in Egypt had the Lord not brought them out of their bondage by His great power, so they should care for the rest of their servants.
The fifth commandment:

With this commandment begin the commandments concerning man's relationship with others, the most important of which is the relationship with his parents. God commands that every person care for his parents and meet their needs, so God prolongs his days on the earth in happiness with God, whether by the length of his life or by his delighting in his life with God. God promises many good things on earth to whoever cares for his parents, and then indescribable good things in the new land, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven. The sixth commandment:

Life is a gift from God; He gave it and He alone takes it, so man's life is sacred and must be respected and not violated in any form, otherwise God commands that the one who does this be punished by death, as He said from the days of Noah (Gen 9:6). The seventh commandment:

Adultery is a hideous sin, called in many places of the Bible "uncleanness," and because of it the Lord punished many peoples, beginning with the Flood and going on to the burning of Sodom and Gomorrah ... and the Lord Christ considered it a sufficient and sole reason for dissolving the holy bond of marriage.
The eighth commandment:

Stealing is taking another's property, and it is most cruel in its effect on others since it deprives them of what they need, and the hideousness of this sin increases if the one stolen from is of the weak classes in society, like the widow and the poor.
The ninth commandment:

If a person's testimony is required in court, he must neither add anything to the truth nor take anything from it, so that he wrongs no one, and show favor to no one, rich or poor (Deut 16:18-20). The tenth commandment:

Covetousness is an inner feeling of the heart and the first stage of the outward act that is to be condemned. Sin begins first in thought, and if we let this thought grow within us, it leads us in the end to the act. Hence the importance of the control of thought, which our Church calls for. This commandment fights sin at its roots, for if we refrain from coveting what belongs to others, we learn contentment and satisfaction.

And He added no more: that is, it needs no addition or increase, for it contains all the other legislation. At the end of his narration of the commandments, Moses the prophet affirms that they are the words of God which He gave him written on two tablets of stone when He appeared on the mountain, on which the glory of God appeared in mist, cloud and fire, and that these are the words of God and nothing is to be added to them.

May we be committed to carrying out God's commandments in our life, however great the pressures around us or the drifting of those around us into various sins, in order that we may enjoy God's care and blessings however much evil surrounds us.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: The heads: the heads of the twelve tribes and their assistants.

The elders: the seventy elders chosen from the people to help Moses (Num 11:16). When the people saw the greatness of God in His appearing with fire and mist on the mountain and also heard His voice, they were greatly afraid, and showed this in their speech with the heads, marveling at the grace of God that allowed them to hear His voice and see Him, because they know that man cannot bear to see God.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: In their great fear they declared to the heads their inability to see God again, lest His fire consume them and they die, because God's appearing is beyond man's capacity.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: The people asked Moses to stand before God and speak with Him and then tell them what He wants, for fear of God's appearing to them again; but at the same time they were ready to obey Him in all that He commands, as Moses would tell them.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: God praised the people's fear of Him and their readiness to obey Him, which they declared with their lips, and hoped that it would be in their hearts so that they would continue in this virtue and it would not be mere passing emotions.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: God agreed to the people's returning to their tents because of their inability to continue seeing the glory of God, and it suffices that Moses stand before Him so that God may tell him the commandments and laws which he would teach the people, that they might live by them throughout their lives when they enter the land of Canaan.

entries.section: (3) The people's fear of facing the Lord

paragraphs.text: Moses the prophet comments at the end, after he had recounted to them what happened at the receiving of the commandments and the Law, and asks the people to hold fast to God's word and carry it out, that they may live in peace and their days be prolonged in the Promised Land, filled with good things.

The fear of God is the beginning of the spiritual life, which ensures for you right conduct in His commandments and keeping away from sin. So always remember the greatness of God who stands before you, and you will live in purity and safety, and evil will not be able to enter you, and in the end you will secure the Kingdom of Heaven.
Doing the commandment

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Before Moses mentions God's commandments and laws to the people, he warns them that the purpose of his words is that they do them after their entering the land of Canaan.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Carrying out God's word is the proof of their godliness, and he reminds them of the importance of doing these commandments not only in their generation but in all the coming generations, so that they may enjoy dwelling and settling in the Promised Land.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: A land that floweth with milk and honey: an expression common among the peoples of that period for the fertility and goodness of the land, which the Promised Land enjoyed, especially in its northern part. He gives them the good news that if they carry out God's commandments exactly, they will obtain many good things and God will bless their number so that they increase and fill the Promised Land.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Before declaring the commandments, he reminds them that God is one, with no partner among the pagan gods, therefore his following words are of the utmost importance. This shows Judaism's call to the oneness of God among the peoples of the world who believe in a multiplicity of gods. Of course this does not conflict with faith in the Holy Trinity, that is, the essential attributes of God. There are indications of the Trinity in the Old Testament, and some see an indication of it in this verse, since the name of God is mentioned three times, as it says, the Lord, our God, the Lord. But the Trinity was declared clearly in the New Testament at the baptism of Christ in the Jordan River (Mt 3:16, 17).

Your faith in the oneness of God generates in you the fear of Him and respect for His commandments and striving to carry them out, and you also feel reassured in His hands because He loves you and there is no other god besides Him, so no one can harm you.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Since God is one and loved His people and cared for them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt and tending them in the wilderness, it is natural that His people love Him with a complete love, which he details as follows:
1- With all thine heart: that is, the feelings.
2- With all thy soul: which includes all of man's spiritual faculties, that is, the mind and the conscience.
3- With all thy might: that is, all of man's bodily, that is outward, capacities.
In sum, the love of God with all of man's energy, inwardly and outwardly. Christ considered this verse the greatest commandment (Mt 22:35-39).

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Moses demands of the people that God's commandments be their life and before their eyes at all times and that they repeat them always, but above all that they keep them in their hearts, so that they cover and contain all their feelings. And if they keep them in their hearts, that is, within them, they appear easily in their words and works.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: since your heart is occupied with them, care to teach them to your children, so that they are established in your heart by your repeating them and your children live in them, and you encourage them and they encourage you to walk by them.

Thou shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: that is, they are to be the first subject in your family life, so you repeat them in your chamber and in your house with your family, for repeating God's word establishes it in your heart, so that it is your first occupation in your inner and private life.

When thou walkest by the way: if you go to your work, do not neglect them but repeat them on the way as you go to your works and your engagements with others, so that they occupy your mind in every place you go to. And when thou liest down: they are to be on your tongue and in your mind even while you are on your bed, so that they are the last thing in your thought, and consequently your dreams and your subconscious mind are also occupied with them.
And when thou risest up: when you wake from sleep, you begin your day by repeating them, so you begin your daily life with them.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: The Jews understood this commandment literally, so they wrote the commandment in small script and put it in a leather case and bound it on their hands. But what is meant is the spiritual meaning, that is, that the commandment cleave to everything to which your hands reach out, so that all your works are according to God's commandments.

And they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: the band is a piece of cloth wound around the head to be like a turban, and the Jews also understood this commandment literally, so they wrote the commandments and put them in a leather case inside this band on the head, indeed they made their bands broad to contain the papers on which these commandments were written. Christ rebuked their concern for the letter of the commandment and their appearance and their neglect of its essence (Mt 23:5). What is meant is that the commandment be in man's thought always, because the head represents the mind.

entries.section: (1) Keeping the commandment and repeating it

paragraphs.text: The posts of thy house: that is, the main columns on which the house stands.
The Jews applied this commandment literally by writing it on the doors and the posts of the house, and what is meant by the gates is:
1- Man's senses, that is, the entrances through which outward thoughts come in to him, so that God's word is the filter that sifts and purifies everything.
2- The doors are what people enter by, so they signify our relationship with others, so that its foundation too is God's word.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: God gives them the good news that they will possess in the land of Canaan cities, buildings, wells of water and lands planted with vines and olive trees which they did not labor to build, dig and plant, so that they may enjoy them and be filled with God's good things.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: God warns them against being preoccupied with these good things when they find their material needs met and are settled, so that they forget Him, and He reminds them of His love, especially when they were in severe distress in Egypt and He brought them out by His power, so that they would not be influenced by the worship of idols or become attached to material things and leave Him.

Thank God for His gifts to you, but use them in measure, and do not indulge in your material lusts and rely on them so that your relationship with God weakens. Fasting and all that is connected with it of prayers and good works is necessary for your salvation.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: God asked three things of them in their relationship with Him after their entering the land, which are:
Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God: so that you fear God and keep away from every sin or anything that angers Him.
And serve Him: offering the ritual worship of prayers and sacrifices and all that the Law prescribed, that their hearts may cling to His love and they may enjoy His blessings.
And shalt swear by His name: that the name of God be the decider in all their disputes and dealings, to protect them from swearing by pagan gods.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: He stresses the need to beware of the worship of the idols which the peoples living around them in the new land worship, because all of them are vain and the works of demons.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: He reminds them of His intense love for them as a bride of His own, for whom He cares and over whom He is jealous; so if they worship idols, the Lord will be angry with them and drive them out of the land of good things which He gave them, and this is what happened in the captivity.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Massah: a place near Rephidim where the people thirsted in the wilderness of Sinai.

He warns them, if they meet any tribulations, not to doubt the power of God who cares for them or His care for them, as they murmured against Him in the wilderness of Sinai when they thirsted in a place called Massah and said, "Is the Lord among us, or not?" (Ex 17:7).

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Therefore he demands of them that they hold fast to His commandments and laws, so that they live in assurance, far from all murmuring and sin.

entries.section: (2) Worshipping God in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Instead of murmuring and sins, God calls them to do good and works of mercy with one another, so God will bless them and they will settle in the Promised Land from which God drove out its inhabitants because of their evil.

entries.section: (3) Teaching children the fear of God

paragraphs.text: After their settling in the Promised Land, their children will notice their attachment to laws that differ from those of the other surrounding peoples, so they will ask their fathers the reason for their difference from the other peoples.

entries.section: (3) Teaching children the fear of God

paragraphs.text: The fathers must explain to their sons God's care for them, by bringing them out of the land of Egypt with His strong hand by means of the ten plagues, then leading them in the wilderness of Sinai, and afterwards giving them possession of the Promised Land filled with good things, therefore they worship Him and hold fast to His commandments and Law, which distinguish them from the other peoples by God's care for them.

May you care to bring up your children spiritually and teach them the love and fear of God, and how to worship Him in the Church and thank Him at all times for His great works with them and His care for them, so that your faith and theirs in God is established in the midst of the wicked world.

entries.section: (3) Teaching children the fear of God

paragraphs.text: Because of God's love and care, fathers teach their children to hold fast to His commandments and laws, so that it is well with them, and God counts that to them as righteousness, and they are established in the Promised Land.

From what has preceded appear God's grace with His people and His redemption of them from Egypt by the Passover lamb, but for the continued enjoyment of God's grace and His salvation, man's striving must appear in his holding fast to God's commandments. Therefore, in proportion to your sense of God's grace, hold fast to His commandments, and offer repentance every day for your sins and reject everything that leads to them.
The worship of God is the cause of His people's victory

entries.section: (1) Not mixing with the pagan peoples

paragraphs.text: The Hittites: the descendants of Heth, the second of the sons of Canaan, who dwelt in scattered countries of the land of Canaan. The Girgashites: one of the tribes of the Canaanites.
The Amorites: of the descendants of Canaan; because of their importance in the land of Canaan their name was sometimes applied to all the Philistines.
The Canaanites: the descendants of Canaan, the fourth son of Ham; they dwelt in every region of the Promised Land, having scattered tribes.

The Perizzites: that is, the villagers; they are older than the Canaanites and dwelt in the north of the Promised Land. The Hivites: they dwelt in Shechem and Gibeon and at the foot of Mount Lebanon, and obtained a covenant of peace from Joshua by deceit.
The Jebusites: one of the tribes of the Canaanites, who dwelt in the region that later became the city of Jerusalem.
God demands things of them after their entering the Promised Land and God's driving out before them seven pagan peoples stronger than they.

It is to be noted that God had promised Abraham to give his descendants the inheritance of ten peoples (Gen 15:19-21), but three of them disappeared and joined others, so there were these seven peoples mentioned here.

entries.section: (1) Not mixing with the pagan peoples

paragraphs.text: Thou shalt utterly destroy them: you shall kill them and wipe them out.

The first demand of God upon His people when they enter the Promised Land is to kill its wicked pagan inhabitants and not have pity on them, because this is God's punishment of them for their evils in which they persisted for many years, and He uses His people as an instrument to carry out this punishment. And this is not a permission to His people to kill any person except these wicked peoples.
The second divine demand is not to make treaties with the pagans but to wipe them out as He commanded.

entries.section: (1) Not mixing with the pagan peoples

paragraphs.text: The third divine demand is no intermarriage between the people of God and the pagan peoples, for it would make the children of God turn aside from His worship and worship the gods of the foreign nations, and then God would punish them and destroy them, as happened in the age of the Judges.

May every person be careful when entering into marriage, and choose the one who helps him in life with God and steadfastness in the Church, that he may obtain God's blessings in his life and be delivered from many problems.

entries.section: (1) Not mixing with the pagan peoples

paragraphs.text: Images: idols and statues.
Groves: the pillars which were set up on high places and mountains, which signified the pagan gods.

But what is required of them is to demolish their altars and break their idols which they worship and remove their pillars which they set up on the mountains as a symbol of their vain gods, and to burn with fire the images they carved for their gods.

God shows the reason for His command not to mix with the pagan peoples, which is that they are a people set apart for His worship and nearer to His heart than all peoples, for they worship Him and keep away from the worship of idols and the evil lusts in which the rest of the peoples walk.

The Lord shows that He did not choose His people the children of Israel because of the greatness of their number, for on the contrary they are among the fewest of peoples, and He chose their father Abraham, who was a single individual without offspring (Gen 12:1-3), then gave him Isaac. He did not take Ishmael as a son although he had twelve sons. And Jacob and his sons who entered Egypt numbered about seventy, and by God's being with them He blessed them despite the tribulations of Egypt and its bondage.
The reasons for God's choosing His people are:
1- His love for them.

2- His oath and covenant to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to bless their descendants; for this reason He rescued them from the bondage of Egypt and delivered them from the hand of Pharaoh, hard of heart.

God's choosing His people is a declaration of His keeping His covenant with the fathers, for He keeps His covenants throughout the generations, since the number thousand points to perfection, and He will continue to care for them on condition of their obedience to Him.

On the other hand, whoever disobeys God and rejects Him, God punishes and destroys him swiftly, that is, he meets troubles in his life on earth and then eternal destruction, for He does not give them respite beyond the length of their life on earth, and destroys them with an eternal destruction, since the length of life is very short in comparison with eternity.
Because God chose His people and loved them, they must then keep His commandments and live by them.

How great is the grace of sonship which God has given you in the sacrament of Baptism! So in order to enjoy His fatherhood and care, obey His commandments, cling to the Church and repent quickly of your sins, that you may keep your sonship to Him.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of keeping the commandments

paragraphs.text: God encourages His people that if they obey His commandments, He will surely be faithful to them in keeping His covenants to their fathers, so He will give them many good things.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of keeping the commandments

paragraphs.text: The Lord enumerates the blessings with which He will overwhelm His people if they choose the way of obedience and keep the commandments, and these blessings are detailed in the following three verses. In this verse the blessings include:
1- Many children.
2- Abundance in the good things of the land, in agricultural produce.
3- Livestock production, and an increase of the ewes on which the abundance of offspring and milk depends.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of keeping the commandments

paragraphs.text: The second kind of blessings is the exaltation of the nation above all kingdoms and communities.

He also promises them a great number and fertility in the bearing of offspring, of men and animals, for the increase in the population of the people means strength in facing the enemy and a deterrent to him, and by the fertility of the animals the people enjoy abundance of food.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of keeping the commandments

paragraphs.text: Diseases: sicknesses like those with which God struck the people of Egypt, such as boils.
The third blessing is God's protection of His people from the diseases that were widespread in Egypt and which they saw with their own eyes, so the people increase in strength.

The blessings of God to His children who obey Him are countless. So do not be dazzled by the success of the wicked, for it is temporary and accompanied by turmoil, while God's blessings to you are suited to you and satisfy you and give you a peace that only the children of God obtain.
A snare: a trap.

God commands them to wipe out the pagan peoples and not to have pity on them, because this is God's punishment of them; for if they spare them, they will be a trap for the people of Israel through their mixing with them and worshipping their idols.

God warns him not to fear the multitude or strength of the pagan peoples living in Canaan, but to trust in the power of God that is with him, and to remember how He rescued him from the strong bondage of Egypt by striking the Egyptians with the ten plagues, and likewise He will strike everyone who is hostile to him in the land of Canaan.
The hornets: plural of "hornet," an insect yellow and black in color.

The literal meaning points to swarms of stinging insects which God will send to harass the peoples with whom Israel will go to war, so they will be a help to him in the victory over those peoples, as in (Josh 24:12). Or God will cause them troubles and harassments as the stings of hornets cause them, so that those who remain, who were not killed by the sword, and those fleeing from the war, perish.
He reassures him that the great God dwells in their midst, so he should not fear the strength of any enemy, for it is nothing before the power of God that is with him.

God declares to His people that they will wipe out the pagan peoples gradually, because if they destroyed them all at once the land would become empty of inhabitants and be filled with wild beasts, and the land would be neglected since there would be no one to cultivate it, and it would lose its fertility. So God destroys the pagans gradually until His people multiply and possess their land, so that the land continues to flow with milk and honey.
The Lord will make them be defeated before them and will make their enemies in turmoil and anxiety before them until they and their kings are wiped out, so no one can stand against the people of God.

Joshua indeed killed thirty-one kings and took their cities (Josh 12:24), in addition to the kings whom the children of Israel killed in the age of the Judges, such as Eglon king of the Ammonites (Judg 3:20, 21) and Jabin king of the Canaanites (Judg 4:21, 24).

God also commands them to smash the idol images and burn them, whatever silver or gold is on them, and not to bring them into their houses, lest their hearts be drawn to worship them like the pagan peoples, and they defile themselves and their houses and God's punishment come upon them by their death as He destroyed the pagan peoples. Indeed He calls them to hate these idols, because God commanded that they be devoted to destruction, that is, destroyed, for their uncleanness.
Reject everything connected with sin and do not keep pictures or belongings associated with evil, lest they remind you of sin in your time of weakness and make you fall into it.

God's care in the wilderness and the punishment for forgetting Him (1) The testing of the people in the wilderness and His care for them (vv. 1-10:) "All the commandments which I command thee this day shall ye observe to do, that ye may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers. 2And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no. 3And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live. 4Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years. 5Thou shalt also consider in thine heart, that, as a man chasteneth his son, so the LORD thy God chasteneth thee. 6Therefore thou shalt keep the commandments of the LORD thy God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him. 7For the LORD thy God bringeth thee into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths that spring out of valleys and hills; 8A land of wheat, and barley, and vines, and fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil olive, and honey; 9A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarcity, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass. 10When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee."

God declares to His people that if they keep His commandments, they will obtain His blessings in the greatness of their number, their possession of the Promised Land and their enjoyment of life with Him.

Although the way from Egypt to Canaan takes no more than a few days, God made them wander in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years to test them and discipline them, so that He might know how firmly they held to His commandments amid the hard conditions of the wilderness of Sinai; and if they succeeded, He would give them the Promised Land.

God tested His people with hunger at the beginning of their journey in Sinai, and when they were about to die, God showed His care for them and sent them manna, which continued to fall every day for 40 years, that they might know that God is the source of their life, since He gave them a delicious food strange to them, which neither they nor their fathers had known before, so that they would love God and His word and do His commandments, indeed prefer them even to their material needs such as bread; or, in other words, know that God is the source of their life by His commandments and also gives them their material needs, that is, food. Christ quoted this verse in His reply to Satan at the temptation (Mt 4:4).

In God's care for His people in the harsh conditions of the wilderness of Sinai, He preserved their clothes so that they did not wear out for 40 years. This is beyond the ability of ordinary cloth to endure for all this time. And He gave their feet strength so that they did not swell from so much walking on the sands of the wilderness and on its mountains. So God, along with the commandment, gives help to make us feel His presence and encourage us to carry out His commandments.

God shows that His discipline of His people by their wandering in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years was not vengeance or cruelty but care and concern, as a father cares for the upbringing of his son and his discipline so that he may be a strong and successful person.

Look at God's care and providence for you, and accept His disciplines in the form of the adverse circumstances you meet in your life, for they are for your good and for correcting your mistakes, and this impels you to repentance and to thanking God for His love.
In view of God's fatherhood and great love, His children must hold fast to His commandments with all exactness and fear Him in their works, so that they walk uprightly.
Depths: the abundant waters that come out of the springs in addition to rainwater. Valleys: the wadis and the various places of the land.
He gives them the good news that the land they will possess enjoys abundant water, which helps its cultivation and fertility and the abundance of the crops it produces.

He mentions a proof of the fertility of the land, which is the variety of its great crops such as wheat and barley, in addition to fruits such as grapes, figs, pomegranates and olives, and likewise it has bees and abundant honey.
Without scarcity: you will eat sparingly for fear of the scarcity of its fruits.
God gives them the good news of abundant crops, so they eat of them as they wish, in addition to the presence in it of mines of metals such as iron and copper.
After they obtain these good things, they must thank God and bless Him; this is the natural response to God's grace.

(2) Not forgetting God (vv. 11-16:) "11Beware that thou forget not the LORD thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day: 12Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; 13And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; 14Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the LORD thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; 15Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint; 16Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not, that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end;"

Before Moses enumerates to them the reasons that may make them turn aside from the Law, he repeats his warning to the people of the necessity of holding fast to the commandment and the judgments and statutes which he charges them with.
He warns them against forgetting God and His worship through preoccupation with the good things of the land, which are:
1- Abundant eating and drinking.
2- Settling in houses and fortified cities.
3- Owning many cattle.
4- Owning silver and gold.

God reminds them of His care for them throughout their journey in the harsh wilderness of Sinai, where He preserved them from the poisonous serpents widespread in the mountains and from scorpions and protected them from the terrors of the land. And despite the dryness of the wilderness of Sinai, God gave them water from the hard flint rocks from which water cannot come, and He also gave them manna from heaven; and although He allowed them to suffer and be humbled so that they would feel the hardship of life, as a result of disobeying God's commandments, at the same time He showed them His kindnesses to them in preserving them and providing for their needs of food and drink, so that they would believe in Him and trust in Him and obey His commandments, to possess in the end the Promised Land and then enter the Kingdom of Heaven after their earthly life.

Beware of being preoccupied with material things instead of God, but thank God for them and use them in measure and remember that they are God's grace to you, so that you take them with thanksgiving and also do not forget His care for you throughout your life.

(3) Pride and the punishment of forgetting (vv. 17-20:) "17Lest thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth. 18But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day. 19And it shall be, if thou do at all forget the LORD thy God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I testify against you this day that ye shall surely perish. 20As the nations which the LORD destroyeth before your face, so shall ye perish; because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the LORD your God."
God warns them not to attribute the good things of the land of Canaan to their own power, in pride and arrogance, when they become rich through the abundance of their possessions.
God calls them to remember Him in prayer, because He is the giver of good things, as He promised their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Thank God every day for His gifts, so your love for Him appears and His blessings overflow upon you. And enjoy the gifts of His that are in your hands, so you live in joy however many tribulations surround you, and spread joy among others, especially those who suffer tribulations.
God warns them that if they leave Him and worship idols and neglect His commandments, He will wipe them out and destroy them.
God gives them an example for guarding against the worship of idols, namely the pagan peoples living in the land of Canaan, whom God will wipe out from before them because of their worship of idols.
The people's disobedience to God

entries.section: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

paragraphs.text: Fenced up to heaven: a figure for the height of the cities' walls and the difficulty of getting past them.
The sons of Anak: they lived in the south of Palestine, between Jerusalem and Hebron, and were described as giants because of their great stature and their strength in war.

God announces to them that they will cross the Jordan River, enter and possess the land of Canaan, which is inhabited by a people of giants who live in fortified cities, the sons of Anak, of whom all the peoples are afraid.

entries.section: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

paragraphs.text: A consuming fire: a destroying power.

He draws their attention to the great power of God, which He likens to a consuming fire that will pass before them, frightening the enemies and supporting His children, so that they will easily be able to overcome their enemies. The secret of the strength of God's people is God's presence with them.

May you attribute every success you achieve to God; rather, let God's grace grow great in your eyes, because it works in your weakness and your difficult circumstances. In this way your faith is made firm and the work of God's power in you increases.

entries.section: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

paragraphs.text: God warns them not to attribute their victory over their enemies to their own righteousness and the wickedness of the enemies. It is God, who is tender toward His people, who gave them this righteousness and forgave them their sins, so they must thank God for His grace toward them and must not be proud.

entries.section: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

paragraphs.text: The victory of God's people did not come because of their righteousness and the uprightness of their conduct, but the reasons for this victory are:
1- The wickedness of the enemies in worshiping idols and in evil lusts.
2- God's promises to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

entries.section: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

paragraphs.text: Stiffnecked: a figurative expression meaning stubborn, resistant and disobedient.

So that God's people would not be proud, He reminds them of their stubbornness and their rebellion against Him, yet God in His longsuffering bears with them and calls them to repentance. Because they believe in Him, they return to Him. In sum, they fall into evil like the enemies, but what distinguishes them is their faith in God and His power working in them.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: You provoked the Lord to wrath: you made the Lord angry.
God draws their attention to the repetition of their disobedience toward Him: they stirred up His anger against them many times throughout their journey in the wilderness of Sinai.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: He reminds them of their worship of the golden calf at Horeb (Ex 32:4); God was angry with them and wanted to destroy them, and many of them were killed by the hand of Moses.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: He reminds them of the incident of the golden calf, when Moses went up the mountain to receive the Ten Commandments written on two tables of stone, and fasted there forty days, and received them from God (Ex 32). They are the very same words that God spoke when He appeared on the mountain in the form of a great fire (Ex 19, 20).

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: At the end of the forty days and forty nights the Lord said to him, "Arise, get thee down quickly," for the people had transgressed the commandment and had made a golden image of a calf and worshiped it.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Let me alone, that I may destroy them: perhaps Moses bowed down before God and began to intercede for his people. This also shows the standing of Moses and of the people with God.

The Lord wanted to destroy the people as a recompense for their disobedience to the commandment and their rebellion against Him, and it became perfectly clear that they were a stubborn and resistant people. He asked Moses not to hold on to them, for He would utterly put an end to them as a nation, and from the descendants of Moses another people, better than they, would arise. Then Moses came down from the mountain with the two tables of the covenant in his hands.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: When Moses saw the people's abandonment of God and their worship of the golden calf, he was very angry and cast down the tables of the Law, and they were broken.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: As at the first: that is, as he pleaded for them the first time, when the Lord commanded him to go down and see the people, who had made themselves a molten image (Ex 32:11). Moses fell down before the Lord, fasting, forty days and forty nights again, as before, pleading before the Lord to forgive the sin of the people.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Moses was terrified at God's anger against his people and begged Him to forgive them, and God answered him. This shows the importance of intercession.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Because Aaron shared with the people in their error, in that he made the golden calf for them (Ex 32:21), the Lord was angry with him and decided to destroy him; but here too the Lord accepted the intercession of Moses and did not destroy Aaron.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Stamped: crushed.

The brook that descended out of the mount: the spring that came out of the rock which he struck at Rephidim (Ex 17:6). Moses took the golden image of the calf that they had made, burned it with fire, crushed it and ground it until it was as fine as dust, and then cast it into the brook that came down from the mountain in that place. The destruction of the calf is a declaration of the necessity of getting rid of sin and destroying it, and the people drank the water mixed with dust so that they would know that they had drunk iniquity like water.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Taberah: that is, burning; it is a place in the wilderness of Paran and the first place mentioned after their departure from Sinai (maps 4, 8).
Massah: that is, temptation; it is a place in the wilderness of Sin, also called Meribah (Ex 17:7), and it is near Rephidim, which is in the valley of Feiran.
Kibroth-hattaavah: that is, the graves of lust; it is a place north of Mount Horeb, in the south of the Sinai peninsula, and it is the place where the murmurers were buried.
Here Moses briefly mentions some other shameful incidents that took place on the part of the people during their long journey in the desert of Sinai.

At Taberah (Num 11:1-3) the people murmured and complained a great deal, so the Lord was angry and a fire was kindled among them and burned the outskirts of the place where they were staying; then Moses prayed to God and the fire was quenched. And at Massah (Ex 17:7), where the people quarreled with Moses over water, he said to them, "Why do ye tempt the LORD?" and he struck the rock, and water came out of it for the people to drink.

And at Kibroth-hattaavah (Num 11) the people murmured, saying, "Who shall give us flesh to eat?" Then a wind went forth from the Lord and brought quails from the sea and let them fall in the place where the people were encamped, and while the meat was still between their teeth the Lord struck them with a very great plague, and there they buried the people who had lusted for meat.

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: And at Kadesh-barnea, there they did not believe the Lord and did not listen to His voice when He asked them to get ready to possess the land, to arise and fight, because they were afraid of the words of the spies who had returned from spying out the land. They were unwilling to attack the inhabitants of the land, although God had reassured them, saying, "Fear not, neither be discouraged," and Moses said to them, "Dread not, neither be afraid of them." Then they sinned a second time when they decided to fight, while the Lord had said to them, "Go not up, neither fight."

entries.section: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

paragraphs.text: Moses knew that they were a disobedient people from his constant companionship with them throughout the journey, and he cited as evidence the events, transgressions and errors that they had committed against the Lord since he took over their leadership, beginning with the Exodus from Egypt, and he confronted them with this judgment of his upon them.

It is good for you to remember your sins which you have confessed and which God has forgiven you, without going into their details, so that you may be humble before God and strive with zeal. Although God has forgiven you your sins, He awaits your love and your seriousness in spiritual striving, and this will make you have compassion on sinners, so that you do not judge them but support them with your love.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of Moses for the people

paragraphs.text: Moses bowed down before the Lord forty days and forty nights to intercede for the people, so that the Lord would not destroy them, and he prayed to the Lord, asking Him to pardon the people and not to destroy them, because they were His people whom He had adopted and acquired for Himself and brought out of Egypt by His surpassing power.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of Moses for the people

paragraphs.text: Moses interceded by the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He asked the Lord to overlook the hardness of this people, their disobedience and their sin.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of Moses for the people

paragraphs.text: Moses prayed to the Lord, saying: May You, O Lord, pardon them, lest the rest of the nations gloat over them and justify the reason for Your destroying them as being Your inability to make them victorious over the peoples of the land that You promised them, and because You hated Your people You decided to wipe them out in the desert.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of Moses for the people

paragraphs.text: And Moses continues his prayer, saying that although the people have sinned, may You, O God, look upon them with a fatherly eye and pardon them, for they are Your people and Your children on whom You had compassion before, when they cried out to You from the humiliation of slavery, and You brought them out by Your mighty strength and Your great power.

God's tenderness is wonderful and surpasses all imagination. So humble yourself before Him with lowliness, and He will forgive you every sin and remove it from you; and intercede by His saints, and they will support you, and you will enjoy a fellowship of love with them and the work of God in you. God's love for His people and their fear of Him

God asked Moses to make two new tables of stone, because Moses had broken the first two, and to go up the mountain so that God might write on them the Ten Commandments, and then Moses was to place them in the ark of the covenant which God had commanded him to make.
Shittim wood: a kind of tree whose wood is heavy and hard and does not rot.

Moses carried out the Lord's instructions and made the ark of shittim wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the two he had broken before, as an expression of his anger at the people, and he went up the mountain with the two tables in his hand.

God wrote the Ten Commandments on the two new tables of stone, and they are the same commandments that He spoke on the day He appeared on the mountain in the form of fire before all the people (Ex 19:17).

Moses departed from before the Lord and came down from the mountain, and put the two tables in the ark of the covenant that Bezaleel made, before the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 25:10). There is another opinion, that Moses made a temporary wooden ark in which he put the two tables until the ark of the covenant and all the contents of the tabernacle were completed.

God in His love is ready to forgive your sins, to renew His covenants with you and to repeat His words to you so that you may live by them. So do not neglect His voice, but show your love, respond to Him and begin anew.

entries.section: (2) The death of Aaron and the setting apart of the tribe of Levi

paragraphs.text: The wells of the children of Jaakan: the children of Jaakan are the name of a tribe descended from Seir, whose name was given to the place that lies 20 km to the northeast of Kadesh-barnea.
Mosera: perhaps it was the valley of Haroniyya; it lies south of Mount Hor and very close to it, and north of the wells of the children of Jaakan (map 16).
Map (16): a map showing the places mentioned in ch. 10, vv. 6, 7, which are:

The children of Jaakan, Mosera, Gudgodah, Jotbath; the locations of these places are not now determined with certainty, and they all lie in the region enclosed between the northern end of the Gulf of Aqaba and Mount Hor to the north.

Moses reminded them that during their journey in the desert, when they passed through the region of the wells of the children of Jaakan and reached the region of Mosera, which is next to Mount Hor, Aaron died there, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as head of the priesthood.

entries.section: (2) The death of Aaron and the setting apart of the tribe of Levi

paragraphs.text: Gudgodah: a region north of the Gulf of Aqaba.
Jotbath: it is thought to be present-day Taba, 9 km southwest of the port of Eilat, on the western shore of the Red Sea.
After the death of Aaron at Mosera (Mount Hor), the people moved to two other places, Gudgodah and Jotbath, and the latter has many sources of water.

entries.section: (2) The death of Aaron and the setting apart of the tribe of Levi

paragraphs.text: When they were in Sinai, and specifically at Horeb, they were given the details of the consecration of the tribe of Levi to the service of the tabernacle of meeting. The priesthood was limited to the sons of Aaron, while the Levites were assigned the following:
1- Carrying the ark of the covenant, by the Kohathites, who are one of the clans of the Levites.
2- To stand before the Lord to serve Him as assistants to the priests.
3- Blessing God and praising His holy name in His house.

Although Levi had sinned with his brother Simeon in the incident of Shechem by killing the men of that tribe (Gen 34:30, 31), his descendants obeyed God, and their zeal appeared in helping Moses to kill the rebels who insisted on worshiping the golden calf (Ex 32:26-29), so God consecrated them to His service.

entries.section: (2) The death of Aaron and the setting apart of the tribe of Levi

paragraphs.text: The Lord's instructions were that no portion of the land be allotted to the tribe of Levi when the land was divided among the tribes. This was because they were consecrated to the service of the Lord and had no time to spend on the worldly work needed for a livelihood; therefore the Lord assigned them a share of the burnt offerings, the sacrifices, the tithes, and the offerings and vows that the people offer to the Lord (Num: 11, 12), and in (ch. 14:27) the Lord says to the people, when they spend and eat, "And the Levite that is within thy gates (in your cities); thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee."

Also in (ch. 18:1, 2): "The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel: they shall eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the LORD is their inheritance." So the meaning of the Lord being their inheritance is what is assigned to them of the fire offerings of the Lord and the offerings of the people.

If you are not consecrating all your time to God like the tribe of Levi, then at least consecrate your heart, that is, let your aim be clear, and it is God .. You do everything for Him and to please Him, and you repent of your sins that anger Him, so that you may be free to praise and glorify Him.

Here Moses returns to the main story that he recounted again in (vv. 1-5), the story of receiving the tables of the Law, and he says that he stayed on the mountain a second time forty days and forty nights, when the Lord accepted his intercession and pardoned the people.
Then the Lord commanded him to set out and to lead the people to enter and possess the land that He had promised to their fathers.
Pray to God for all who are distressed and those who are far away, however much they refuse God, for He wants the salvation of all and rejoices in your prayer for them.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: After God showed His care and forgiveness for His people, He requires of them the following, so that they may continue to enjoy His care:
1- The fear of God, which makes them keep away from the worship of idols and from every evil.
2- Obedience to His commandments and orders that He declared to Moses.
3- Love for Him, thanksgiving, and attachment to Him.
4- Worship of Him according to what He made clear to Moses, with sacrifices, prayers and the various purifications.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Keeping the commandments and statutes is not a heavy burden that God places on His people, but is God's grace for the benefit and good of His people, for it gives them inner peace, success in their dealings and many blessings that they receive because of God's pleasure in them.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Moses shows the grace of God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them, how in His love He chose the people of Israel and distinguished them by His care for them because of the fathers' faith in Him and the readiness of the sons, their descendants, to obey Him.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Circumcise the foreskin of your heart: circumcision is the cutting of a part of a person's flesh, which God commanded as a symbol of cutting off sin and evil inclinations. The circumcision of the heart here is meant as purifying the heart from sin so that God may live. Be no more stiffnecked: stiffnecked means extreme stubbornness and resistance to God.
God requires of them to purify their hearts from evil and not to rebel and be stubborn with Him, but to obey His commandments.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Regardeth not persons: He shows favoritism to no one, even if he holds a position.

What shows that God deserves the obedience of His people is that He is above all gods, that is, everything that human beings consider gods and rulers; His power appeared in striking the gods of the Egyptians with the ten plagues and in His dividing the Red Sea, in addition to His justice, for He shows favoritism to no one as human beings do, nor does He pervert justice by taking a bribe, because He is perfect and in need of no one.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: God is distinguished not only by being stronger than all the gods, but also by being merciful and caring for the weak, such as the widow, the fatherless and the stranger, and giving them their rights and tending them.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: The tender God calls them to show kindness to strangers, remembering that they were strangers in the land of Egypt, that is, to feel for strangers and have compassion on them.

May you care for the weak of every kind, whether the poor, the sick or anyone who suffers weakness in his personality, so that you respect everyone and support and encourage them, remembering God's tenderness and mercy toward your own weakness.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Israel must fear God and offer Him the worship that is fitting, cleave to the Lord and continue in communion with Him, and not let the name of another god come to his tongue when he swears.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: Great and terrible things: the ten plagues that terrified the Egyptians.
And he must take pride in the Lord, for He is the One who performed the glorious saving works to bring him out of slavery, of which the people were eyewitnesses.

entries.section: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

paragraphs.text: And God fulfilled His promise to Abraham to make his descendants as many as the stars of heaven, whereas they were a small number of people, not exceeding seventy souls, when Jacob and his sons, the fathers of the tribes, came to Egypt in the days of Joseph's rule.
Review your life from time to time to know how much good the Lord has done for you, more than you ask or think, so that you may live a life of evil and constant joy.
The recompense for obeying the commandment and for disobeying it

Moses stresses to the people that they must love God and keep His commandments, for this is the basis of their stability, their security and all the blessings they receive. This is the same as what Christ said: "If ye love me, keep my commandments" (Jn 14:15).

Moses declares to his hearers that he means those who were children under twenty years of age but were aware of the events in Egypt, that is, the ten plagues and the crossing of the Red Sea, and then all that happened in the wilderness of Sinai, and who did not die in Sinai with their fathers, who refused to enter the Promised Land and were those over twenty years of age. In these words he is not addressing those who were born in the wilderness of Sinai, nor those who were infants and small children not yet aware when they left Egypt, because he is speaking of events they saw that show the recompense of obedience or disobedience.
Moses addresses those who saw the ten plagues in Egypt, which proclaim that He is the only God who must be obeyed.
He made flow over: the waters of the sea rose and flowed over the army of the Egyptians.
He reminded them of His punishment of the Egyptians, who went out after God's people and were drowned in the Red Sea.

Moses also reminds them of God's works with them in the wilderness of Sinai, such as His punishment of Dathan and Abiram, of the tribe of Reuben, and those with them, who joined Korah in murmuring against Moses and Aaron because they alone held the priesthood (Num 16); the earth was cleft and swallowed them up, together with their families and their possessions. All these works of God they saw with their own eyes, and therefore they ought to obey His commandments and not disobey Him.

Remembering the punishment of the wicked and their end warns us to keep away from sin, which seems attractive but is very evil and destroys whoever practices it, and this makes us keep away from everything that leads to it.

entries.section: (2) The good things of the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: The people were on the threshold of the Promised Land, so Moses draws their attention to the importance of obeying the word of God, so that they may possess the new land and settle in it for many years and enjoy its good things, symbolized by milk and honey.

entries.section: (2) The good things of the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: Wateredst it with thy foot: he moves the mud aside with his foot and opens the irrigation channels inside the field, and after these basins are watered he closes the channels with his foot with an amount of mud, so that the water is diverted to the next basins to water them. Plains: the valleys.

God declares to them that the way of watering the land in Egypt depends on the waters of the Nile, which water it easily like fields planted with vegetables. But in the land of Canaan most agriculture depends on the rain water that God gives in its season, which makes people depend on God who gives it. So when they obey Him, His blessings pour down on them from heaven throughout the year, and the land is filled with crops and good things.

One of the loveliest phrases of this book is the phrase "The eyes of the LORD thy God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year." How much the Lord cares for us and provides for our needs, not only at certain moments but throughout all the days of our life on this earth; He knows all our material needs and supplies them to us at the right time. May we in our prayers seek first the Kingdom of God, confident of God's care for us, for He gives us more than we ask or think.

entries.section: (2) The good things of the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: The first rain: at the beginning of the winter planting season, that is, in the month of October, so that the seed may grow.
The latter rain: before the harvest, that is, in the month of March, to complete the growth of the plants.
Grass: fodder plants such as clover.

If you obey God's commandments, He gives you the rains in their due time needed for the growth of the plants, and you will obtain abundant crops of wheat, grapes and olives. The fodder plants needed to feed the animals also grow, so that they become big and fat, which provides all the food needed by God's people.

entries.section: (2) The good things of the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: Be deceived: be tricked and lust.

He warns them against the worship of idols, lest they think that they are the cause of the good things of the land of Canaan, as the pagan peoples living around them say; for then God withholds the rain, and the land dries up and does not yield its crops, and man hungers and perishes.
Here he repeats what he mentioned in (ch. 6:6-9), which is the importance of remembering God's word and repeating it all day long.
As the days of heaven upon the earth: that is, forever; what is meant is a long life.

God gives him the good news that if he obeys the commandment which he repeats all day long, He will grant him a long life in the Promised Land and afterward life in the new land, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

God promises them that if they love Him, obey His commandments and walk by them, He will drive out the pagan peoples, the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, from before them and will give them possession of their land, even though these are strong and great peoples.
Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: a figure for their not being forced to withdraw from any lands they take possession of.
The uttermost sea: the Mediterranean Sea.

An incentive and encouragement from the Lord to them to advance forward without fear of retreat or defeat before the enemies. What they take possession of in lands they will not lose, but they will continually advance forward from victory to victory.
And the Lord defines for them the boundaries of the land promised to them as follows:
On the south, the wilderness, that is, the wilderness of Sinai.
On the north, the mountains of Lebanon.
On the east, the river Euphrates.
On the west, the Mediterranean Sea.
(Note: Israel did not reach this extent except in the reign of Solomon (1 Kgs 4) (map 17).

No military commander who fights you will be able to hinder your advance. And the news of your swift, decisive victories in the battles you wage will be spread, which makes the peoples in the region fear you and tremble at meeting you.

Obeying God's commandments gives you awe in the eyes of those around you, so that they fear to wrong you and respect your word, and you have an opportunity to teach them God's word through your conduct and your ordinary words.
The Lord places Israel at a crossroads to choose between two ways that cannot be combined: a way that leads to enjoying the divine blessings, and a way that brings the curse.
The first way is the way of obedience to the commandments that Moses conveyed to them from the Lord, which he always reminds them of and repeats to them again today.
The second way, in which many curses befall them, is their neglect of God's commandments and their abandoning the worship of Him for the worship of strange gods, that is, idols.
Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal: two mountains south and north of Nablus (Shechem), separated by a narrow valley.

After you enter and possess the land which the Lord leads you to take, stand between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. From these two places, which lie in the middle of the Promised Land, the blessing and the curse are proclaimed, as though the two mountains stood as silent witnesses to the renewal of the covenant.
The blessings and the curses are mentioned in detail in (ch. 27:11-26).
Beyond Jordan: the western side of the Jordan.

A detailed description of the location of the two mountains, Gerizim and Ebal: they are on the western side of the Jordan River, while Moses and the people were standing on its eastern side. From the place where Moses and the people stood, they could see the sun as it sets and disappears behind the two mountains.
Behind the way where the sun goeth down: that is, toward the west.

In the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign: the Arabah is the low valley on the two banks of the Jordan River north of the Dead Sea (map 18). Over against Gilgal: the land of Gilgal is about 13 km north of Bethel. What is meant here is the other region.
The plains of Moreh: the site of the great oak tree where Abraham pitched his tent when he entered Canaan (Gen 12:6), near Shechem.
Map (18)

For you are about to cross the Jordan to take possession of the land which God has given you. Your permanent settlement in this land depends on your care to complete the statutes which I commanded you and to apply the judgments which I have set for you.

With the end of the eleventh chapter, the second sermon of Moses the prophet ends, which began at the end of the fourth chapter from (v. 44). This sermon spoke as a whole about keeping the commandments and keeping away from what hinders them.

God wants to bless your life if you walk with Him and keep His commandments, so do not reject Him for the evils of the world or its passing delights, and do not persist in sin in contempt, exposing yourself to His divine punishment; for despite His constant mercy, He is also perfect in His justice.
The offerings in the house of the Lord

entries.section: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

paragraphs.text: From this chapter on, various laws are mentioned, and in this chapter he concentrates on the worship of God and the offerings presented to Him. From here begins the third sermon of Moses the prophet, which extends to (ch. 27:10) and speaks about the laws and ordinances that must be applied when they enter the land of Canaan, and this sermon is considered the core of the book.

entries.section: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

paragraphs.text: God commands His people to remove every trace of the worship of idols, whether on the mountains, the hills or under the trees.

entries.section: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

paragraphs.text: Pillars: stone columns set up for idols.
Groves: wooden columns set up for idols.

The Book of Deuteronomy. God continues His discourse about removing the worship of idols, and commands that the pagan altars, images and pillars be destroyed and the groves burned. Removing the idols is necessary to purify the people's thought so that they may worship God, the only God.

entries.section: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

paragraphs.text: To put his name: to declare Himself.
His habitation: in it the divine presence and holiness.

He commands them, in their worship of God, not to set up images for Him as the worship of idols is done everywhere, but in the place that God appoints they are to offer communal worship, and not in any other place. What is meant by this is:
1- Affirming the oneness of God and rejecting the idea of a multiplicity of gods, such as a Baal for every pagan city.
2- The unity of the people in their worship of God.
3- Keeping them away from the worship of idols that is widespread around them among the pagan peoples.

entries.section: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

paragraphs.text: Burnt offerings: sacrifices that are burned entirely.
Sacrifices: what is slaughtered of the animals of the offerings.
Tithes: a proportion of one to ten of income, which was required to be offered to the Lord and given to the priests and the Levites.
Heave offerings of your hand: the offerings and oblations that are lifted up to the Lord.
Vows: what a person pledges between himself and himself to offer to God if his request is fulfilled.

Freewill offerings: voluntary offerings (more than the Law requires) that a person offers out of love for God. Firstlings of your herds and of your flocks: the first-born of the animals that are offered to God.
Ye and your households: your wives, your sons and your servants.
