The people must offer their various offerings in the place that the Lord appoints, and what was eaten of them was eaten before the Lord, that is, in His presence. This was an occasion for joy and gladness and for giving thanks to the Lord for all His gifts, blessings and graces which He pours out upon His people.

God's love and humility shine forth in His being present in His Church, waiting for His people to come to Him. So hasten to the bosom of the Church to enjoy the presence of God and to pour out your love and all your needs before Him, and you will receive an inexpressible blessing.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: Here this day: that is, in the wilderness of Sinai.
The rest and the inheritance: that is, the land of Canaan.

The application of the Law in the wilderness of Sinai differed from its application in the land of Canaan, where all the feasts are held and the people are not bound to sprinkle the blood of any sacrifice they slaughter for eating on God's altar, as used to happen in Sinai because of the distance between their dwellings and God's altar.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: He stresses to them that after they enter the land of Canaan, finish their wars, take possession of the land and settle in it, they must be committed to offering all their offerings to the Lord in the place that God appoints for His house, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, so that they and their families may rejoice in the worship of God and eat of the sacrifices, they and the Levites who take their share of these sacrifices and offerings.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: He repeats a second time that the offering of sacrifices and offerings must be in the house of the Lord, whose place God appoints in one of the tribes of the children of Israel, that is, in the land they will possess, and no sacrifices are to be offered in any other place. He stresses this matter many times because, sadly, after they entered and took possession, and after the death of Joshua, the Book of Judges tells us that they were not committed to this, but each one did what he saw fit (Judg 17:6, 21:5).

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: Within any of thy gates: all your houses.
The roebuck: the male gazelle.
The hart: the mountain buck, a kind of mountain goat resembling gazelles, which runs swiftly and has great need of drink and food or else its body grows faint.

The unclean: animals that are clean but are not permitted to be offered as sacrifices to God, since God specified what is offered to Him, such as the bull, the sheep and the goat. It can also mean a person who has been made unclean by any cause, such as an issue of blood or the like.

When they slaughtered any animal to eat in the wilderness of Sinai, they sprinkled its blood on the altar because of the nearness between the tents and the altar, but after they took possession of the land of Canaan, some of the tribes dwelt far from the altar, so God permitted them to slaughter animals for eating from among the clean animals, whether those permitted to be offered to God or not, and to pour out their blood on the ground and cover it with dust, as mentioned in (Lev 17:13). He also permits the eating of this meat to the clean person or to one who has been made unclean by any cause, because it is merely food and not a sacrifice offered to God.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: He repeats a third time that the offering of tithes, firstfruits, vows, freewill offerings and heave offerings must be in the house of the Lord only, and the one who offers it eats of what the Law permits him, he and his family, his servants and the Levites, before the house of the Lord in the holy place and not in his own house.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: The Lord warns not to neglect the Levite's share of the offerings and tithes, for since he was not given a portion of the land like the rest of the tribes, he has a right to the good things of the land like the rest of his brethren of the other tribes, in that he eats his share of the offerings and sacrifices offered to God.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: The LORD thy God shall enlarge thy border: you took possession of the land of Canaan with its wide boundaries.

Here he confirms what he mentioned in (v. 15), that after they possess the land of Canaan and dwell in places far from the house of the Lord, they may slaughter clean animals in their homes to eat of them, whether those permitted to be offered to the Lord or those not permitted, and the clean person or the unclean may eat of them.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: He stresses again that the blood is not to be drunk when animals are slaughtered to be eaten as ordinary food in their homes; they are to pour out their blood on the ground and cover it with dust and not drink of it, for the following reasons:
1- Blood represents the life of the animal, which God created, so out of respect for this life granted by God, they do not drink it.
The Book of Deuteronomy

2- It is a type of the blood of Christ, so they do not drink it, in sanctification of it; and in the New Testament the blood of Christ is given to the believers as life for them through the sacrament of Holy Communion.
3- Drinking blood stirs up a person's lusts and instincts.
4- Blood transmits some diseases, so not drinking it protects against them.
5- So that they may not share with the pagans who drink blood in some of their worship.
And when they obey this commandment, they receive many blessings and good things.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: Thy holy things: the sacrifices offered and set apart for God.

Here too he confirms that the offering of sacrifices to God is to be in His house, in the place that He appoints in the land of Canaan. The blood of the animals is poured out on the altar, and those who offer the sacrifices eat of them in the holy place in the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

paragraphs.text: God confirms His promises of blessings to His people if they obey these commandments.

God cares for the food of His children and not only for their worship. So abide in your relationship with God, confident of His providence and care for all your affairs, and keep His commandments with precision, and you will receive countless blessings.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: After God destroys the pagan inhabitants of the land from before His people and they possess their land, He warns them against taking part in the worship of their idols and inquiring about its details in order to imitate them.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: He forbids them to imitate the methods of pagan worship, for they are defiled methods which the Lord abhors, among them offering human sacrifices of their sons and daughters as offerings to the pagan gods.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: God warns them to carry out His commandments with all exactness, neither adding to them nor taking from them for any personal purpose.
Do not imitate the people of the world in their evil words and their wrong methods, but keep yourself pure in thought, word and deed, because you are the light of the world and the salt of the earth.

Putting to death whoever turns the people away from the worship of God (1) The false prophet (vv. 1-5:) 1 "If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder, 2 And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them; 3 Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for the LORD your God proveth you, to know whether ye love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul. 4 Ye shall walk after the LORD your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him. 5 And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the LORD thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee."

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: A sign: a token.
A wonder: a miracle.

A warning of a danger that could make Israel fall into disobedience, which is the appearance of a false prophet, or one who claims to be a man of visions and dreams, and his attempt to prove the truth of his claims by some miraculous deeds.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: He forbids following the false prophet in turning away from God, even if his prophecy comes true or he works a dazzling miracle, for all this is a deception of Satan.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: God permits these false claims of prophecies and dreams in order to test His people, whether they remain firm in faith in Him or leave Him, because the true believer in God does not let anything draw him away from Him, however great it may be. Magicians appeared in the Old Testament such as Jannes and Jambres in the days of Moses (2 Tim 3:8), and Simon and Bar-Jesus in the days of the Apostles (Acts 8:9, 13:6-11).

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: He calls them to walk in the way of the Lord and in His fear, to keep His commandments, to obey Him, to hold fast to His worship and to cleave to Him all their days.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The false prophet and dreamer who tries to lead the people astray and draw them away from God must be put to death, in order to root out evil and preserve the faith of the people.

Hold fast to your faith which you learned in the Church, however much the wicked try to make you doubt it; on the contrary, read the spiritual books that explain the faith to you and apply this faith in your life, and you will feel God and He will bless you in all your ways.

(2) The wicked relatives (vv. 6-11:) 6 "If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers; 7 Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth; 8 Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him: 9 But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people. 10 And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. 11 And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you."

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The enticement may come from a full brother, a son, a daughter, a wife or a friend dear to you, that is, from your closest relatives, calling you to worship false, pagan gods of which you have not experienced any work in your life and which had no influence on your affairs, either for you or for your fathers, gods that the other peoples worshiped in the regions around you or in the countries far from you, throughout the length and breadth of the earth. This reminds us of what happened with the wives of King Solomon when they enticed him to worship strange gods.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Do not listen to this relative who tries to draw you away from God, and do not pity him, for he will lead many astray if you leave him, and do not conceal his sin because of its gravity and his persistence in it. So after it is confirmed, he must be put to death; he is to be stoned with stones, and your hand is to be the first to cast a stone at him, and then the people, in order to root out evil, so that God may be pleased with you.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The reason for this death sentence is this relative's attempt to draw Israel away from the worship of his God, who brought him out of the slavery of Egypt. In this way he becomes a lesson to any other person who is tempted in his own mind to entice the people onto a path far from their God, and fear fills everyone's hearts.

Do not agree to evil if it comes to you from one of those close to you, and do not flatter him, but be strong in refusing evil and do not take part in it even if this relative is displeased with you, for pleasing God is more important than pleasing people. In this way you save your soul and alert this relative, perhaps he will repent.

(3) The apostasy of a city from God (vv. 12-18:) 12 "If thou shalt hear say in one of thy cities, which the LORD thy God hath given thee to dwell there, saying, 13 Certain men, the children of Belial, are gone out from among you, and have withdrawn the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which ye have not known; 14 Then shalt thou enquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought among you; 15 Thou shalt surely smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein, and the cattle thereof, with the edge of the sword. 16 And thou shalt gather all the spoil of it into the midst of the street thereof, and shalt burn with fire the city, and all the spoil thereof every whit, for the LORD thy God: and it shall be an heap for ever; it shall not be built again. 17 And there shall cleave nought of the cursed thing to thine hand: that the LORD may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and shew thee mercy, and have compassion upon thee, and multiply thee, as he hath sworn unto thy fathers; 18 When thou shalt hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, to keep all his commandments which I command thee this day, to do that which is right in the eyes of the LORD thy God."

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Children of Belial: that is, sons of evil who lead the people of Israel astray from God.
If wicked men appear in one of the Jewish cities and lead the whole city astray from God and decide to worship one of the pagan gods, they must be punished severely.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: So you must first examine the matter with all care and verify that it has really happened and that the report which came to you is true and certain, for this means that this shameful thing which does not please God has actually been done.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Destroying it utterly: you kill and wipe out everything in it and take nothing from it for yourself.

So pass sentence of destruction on the inhabitants of that city, and the whole city and all its goods are to be burned with fire, and its inhabitants and their cattle are to be destroyed, put to the sword, so that the city becomes a heap of dust and is left a ruin and is not rebuilt afterward.

entries.section: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The sentence of putting cities under the ban required the destruction of the city with everything in it without exception, and no one of the people of Israel was to take anything from it for himself (this reminds us of what happened with Achan the son of Carmi, who violated this commandment at the conquest of the city of Ai and took something for himself from Jericho, which was under the ban, so the people stoned him (Josh 7:35, 36). In this way the curse falls upon it, and the anger of the Lord is quenched and He grants you mercy and multiplies your number and blesses you as He swore to your fathers, as long as you keep His commands and carry them out with all exactness.

Keep away from evil places that cause you to stumble, and do not keep anything that could make you fall into sin, and know that a single evil picture that you are careless about looking at can trouble you for many days, and be sure that your relationship with God is more precious than any passing material desire.
The permitted, the forbidden and the tithes
Cut yourselves: wound yourselves.
Baldness between your eyes: shaving the eyebrows because of grief.

God was careful that His people should keep away from the pagans and not imitate them in any practices they perform to please the pagan gods. When the pagans died they would wound their bodies, and this is against respect for the body which God created; likewise they would shave their eyebrows, and this also changes the form of the human being which God created. So He required His people not to do such practices, so that they might keep their sonship to Him and enjoy His care for them.

God reminds them that they are holy and set apart for His worship and must keep away from pagan worship. They are a people special to God, distinct from the rest of the peoples and higher than they, because of their worship of God and His presence among them.

Your distinction from all those around you is in God's dwelling within you, so do not imitate the world in its evil speech and conduct, lest you anger God and hinder His work in you, and examine yourself every day to be purified from the thoughts of the world.

entries.section: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

paragraphs.text: To begin with, the Lord asks them to have clean food, so that the believer may always think of purity and holiness even in his eating and drinking, so he had to distinguish between permitted and forbidden foods.

entries.section: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

paragraphs.text: The Lord specifies for them the clean animals, which are:
1- The ox.
2- The sheep.
3- The goat.
4- The hart: a kind of mountain buck.
5- The roebuck: the male gazelle.
6- The fallow deer: an animal resembling the gazelle and tending to a reddish color.
7- The wild goat: the mountain buck.
8- The pygarg: the wild bull.
9- The wild ox: a kind of wild cattle.
10- The chamois: the wild cow.

entries.section: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

paragraphs.text: Cloven hoof: the nail.

Cheweth the cud: it keeps food in a special place in the stomach and then brings it back to the mouth to chew it. The permitted animal is distinguished from the forbidden by the following two conditions:
1- A split hoof. 2- Chewing the cud.
This has already been mentioned in (Lev 11:3).

entries.section: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

paragraphs.text: If the animal chews the cud but its hoof is not split, it is not eaten, such as the camel, the hare and the coney, an animal resembling the hare but without a tail, which lives in burrows. Likewise it is not eaten if its hoof is split but it does not chew the cud, such as the swine. The flesh of these animals is not eaten and their carcasses are not touched. There is more than one direct reason for the prohibition of eating some animals. Modern studies have proved that eating the flesh of some animals results in health hazards because the food of those animals is poisonous grasses; in addition, some of those animals were associated with pagan practices, some being used as sacrifices to idols such as the camel, and some being pagan symbols of certain ancient societies, so God wanted to set His people apart so that they would not share with the Gentiles in their abominations. Whatever the reasons, the application of this distinction between the clean and the unclean shows the people's obedience to God and their readiness to fulfill the requirements of the covenant with Him.

Not touching the carcasses of the forbidden animals is because they make unclean whoever touches them, and from the health standpoint they may transmit some diseases. Besides the direct reasons, there are symbolic spiritual meanings:

Chewing the cud applies to the believer, in the spiritual sense, who feeds on the living word of God when he always reads God's word and rereads it and meditates on it, as David says in his Psalms: "Blessed is the man ... in the law of the LORD doth he meditate day and night" (Ps 1:2). As for the splitting of the hoof, it means the believer who is led in his life by the spirit of discernment, so he distinguishes between what is suitable for his spiritual and eternal life and what is not beneficial, and avoids conduct in it and sets it aside. It also means the ability to bear weariness, and so signifies spiritual striving.

In Christianity, after the spiritual symbols were understood, it became permitted to eat all the animals that a person wants, as appeared in Peter's vision (Acts 10:11), because God created everything blessed and we keep away only from sin; and of foods we abstain from blood and what is strangled (Acts 15:20).
Much meditation on the word of God purifies a person, so make it a daily food for yourself on which you meditate again and again.

entries.section: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

paragraphs.text: Scales: the scales.
The standard of what is permitted among sea animals is the presence of fins and scales; what has no fins and scales is forbidden and is not eaten because it is unclean.

An example of this is the eel, since it has neither fins nor scales, so it is among the forbidden sea animals. There is a health reason for this, which is that the shelled animals feed on filth, which may cause some diseases.
The spiritual symbolic meanings of this are:
Just as fins help in swimming, so the believer in the world is surrounded by currents opposed to his spiritual course, so he must strive and not yield to the currents of evil.
As for the scales, they are a protection for fish, as the grace of God protects us in our spiritual striving.
Beware of forgetting the means of grace such as repentance, confession, Communion, prayer and reading the Holy Bible, for without them you are drawn to the current of the world and go along with it.
The Law permitted the eating of clean birds, and at the same time in the following verses it forbids the birds that are forbidden to eat, as also mentioned in (Lev 11:13-25).
The forbidden birds that He forbids them to eat are:
The eagle: a large wild bird that seizes its prey; it symbolizes theft.

The ossifrage (al-anuq): called the bearded one, it resembles the eagle and throws its victim down from a height to smash it; it symbolizes cruelty. The osprey: a coastal bird that eats fish; it symbolizes seizing.

The kite: a wild bird that lives by seizing and eating stinking carcasses and feeds on filth. The sparrowhawk: a wild bird of prey like the kite, sharp of sight. It symbolizes the use of talents for evil. The raven: a wild bird that seizes prey and loves stinking carcasses; it symbolizes theft and greed. The ostrich: a huge wild bird that does not sit on its eggs in the nest; it symbolizes recklessness and not bearing responsibility.
The male ostrich: the male of the ostrich, more beautiful than the female. It symbolizes vain outward beauty. The gull: the seagull, a sea bird that snatches; it symbolizes theft and greed.
The hawk: like the falcon, it is used in hunting and symbolizes injustice.
The owl: a wild night bird, and it symbolizes ruin because it lives in ruins.
The cormorant: a coastal bird that dives to seize fish; it symbolizes theft.
The crane: a large long-legged bird that cries out much, and it symbolizes noise and restlessness. The pelican: a strong bird of prey that loves to swim; it symbolizes ferocity.
The quq: a water bird like the swan, and it symbolizes ruin.
The vulture: a bird of prey like the eagle, and it symbolizes evil.
The stork: a bird that eats frogs and insects, with a long beak and long legs. It symbolizes uncleanness and lack of discernment.
The parrot: a predatory bird that imitates speech, and it symbolizes light-mindedness.

The hoopoe: a skillful wild bird that eats worms and insects, and it symbolizes hypocrisy and outward beauty. The bat: among the flying mammals, a bird of prey, and some kinds of it suck blood; it symbolizes parasitism.

He defines the traits of the unclean birds as being predatory, fierce in nature, and eating carrion, that is, stinking carcasses and filth, despite the beauty of their outward appearance. They point to the traits of the wicked and their hypocrisy, as mentioned in the preceding description of the birds, and they show the necessity of the purity of the source of our teaching and our spiritual food, and the necessity of gentleness and of not wronging others.
Creeping: the insects that fly and at the same time walk on the ground, that is, creep upon it.

Flying insects in general are forbidden to eat, except some that are permitted to eat, which are not mentioned here but are mentioned in (Lev 11:21, 22), namely the locust, the bald locust, the beetle and the grasshopper (all of them species of locust). We note that these insects have strong hind legs which help them to leap.
Insects in general feed on filth, so they are defiled, which points spiritually to the person immersed in defiled deeds who lives his life by eating of them.
Those with strong hind legs signify spiritually the believer who is lifted out of his falls, impelled by his longings to rise toward heavenly things.

Clinging to earthly things and constantly thinking about them defiles a person and gradually turns his thoughts to evil. So look always to heaven and take care of your prayers with the saints, and you will rise in your life above sin and above passing material things and rejoice in fellowship with God.

The death of a person takes him to Hades because of sin, since Christ had not yet accomplished redemption in the Old Testament; therefore touching carcasses defiles, and of course eating the carcasses of animals defiles, to declare the gravity of sin which led to the death of man and animal. Although the animal did not sin, it became defiled and its carcass became unclean because of man, who was defiled by sin. The prohibition of eating carcasses came also for health reasons, for eating the flesh of carcasses exposes a person to infection or poisoning; and at present the food-control laws of the state's agencies forbid the sale of the meat of carcasses. As for the matter of giving it to the stranger who dwells among them or selling it to a foreigner, it added nothing to what already existed, since the pagan peoples did not forbid the eating of carcasses, and the Law came to the people set apart for the Lord, whom He separated from among the peoples to be a holy possession, by which they rise above the abominations of the other peoples.
There is a symbolic meaning to this prohibition, which is that the Lord wants the believers to turn away from dead things and always to feed on the life-giving word of God.

As for the second part of this verse, which is the prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk, which was also mentioned in (Ex 23:19), God wants to teach His people kindness to the irrational creation, for God does not want the heart of the mother (the goat) to be broken over her young one in the first period of its nursing, which the infant also needs, for the instinct of motherhood is very strong toward the young (in animals) before weaning, and it lessens gradually afterward.

entries.section: (4) The tithes and the annual firstlings

paragraphs.text: Thy corn: your wheat.

The Lord commanded His people to set apart a tenth of what an individual obtains of the good things of the land, which are the wheat, the grape juice and the oil, and likewise the firstborn of the cattle and sheep he owns, as an acknowledgment by the believer that the Lord is the true owner of the land and all that is on it, and therefore what a person owns is a gift from the Lord, and the one who offers the tithes must bring them to the temple, where they are offered in the form of love feasts (agape) in which the one who offers them shares with others. In this way a person eats with his family and with the poor and thanks God.

entries.section: (4) The tithes and the annual firstlings

paragraphs.text: If the dwelling place of the one who offers the tithes is far from the temple, so that it is hard for him to transport the offerings and walk with them long distances to reach the temple, he may sell them and go with their price to the temple and spend it there on buying cattle, sheep and grape juice to hold the communal feast there, in which the members of his household and the Levite who lives with him in his city share with the one who offers the tithes. The Lord stressed the necessity of not forgetting the Levite because he did not own land like the rest of the tribes. The commandment joined the holding of the feast with joy, for it is joy in the favors of the Lord, who is the giver of all these good things and has poured out His generosity and bounty on us and on those around us. And the eating of the tithes by the one who offers them together with the Levites is a showing of fellowship of love and sympathy with them and a keeping away from any haughtiness on the part of the one who offers the tithes because of what he has given. And going to the temple every year to offer the tithes is a means the Law uses to bind all the believers to the temple of God and His worship, so they offer the tithes there.

entries.section: (4) The tithes and the annual firstlings

paragraphs.text: Every three years the system of distributing the tithes differs, as the third year is the share of the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, so no one takes anything of it to the place of the temple, but it is kept in the cities where those who offer the tithes live and is devoted to meeting the needs of the groups mentioned. The Lord attaches to the commandment a promise that if it is followed, He blesses all the works that the one who offers it does, so that he has much good; by the blessing of the tenth, the other nine tenths are blessed. And his not going to the temple in the third year and distributing the tithes to the needy in his city helps him to care for the sick and the infirm who are unable to go to the temple.
Take care to offer the tithes in order to thank God for His gifts and rejoice with the needy and receive many blessings; indeed, the more your love increases, the more your gifts exceed the tithes.
The seventh year and the firstborn of the animals
Release: freeing or loosing.
God commanded His people to waive the debts owed to them by their brethren every seventh year (Lev 25:

It is called the Lord's release: in the seventh year God commands a release from all debts. He explains the meaning of the release, which is waiving all debts owed by companions and brethren, that is, by all of God's people.

The Law allowed them to demand that non-Jews pay their debts, so the rule of release in the seventh year does not apply to them, out of the Lord's care that the Jews should not be exploited by the cunning of the other peoples, who might borrow from them in bad faith with the aim of not repaying the debt, so that the wealth of the nation would gradually be lost; whereas the debts of the Jews to one another fall within the bounds of the nation itself, and if they are cancelled nothing of it is lost to the outside.

The preceding verses speak about the poor borrowing from their rich brethren. But if there is no poor person among God's people because of God's blessing on all in the land of Canaan, there will be no debts. But if someone borrowed for a sudden financial crisis and then returned and became rich, or borrowed to invest, he must repay the debts in the seventh year.

The blessings are conditional on the people's obedience to God's commandments, by listening to them and doing them, so that they do not withhold help from the needy among their people. Then they will be able to lend to the other nations while they themselves do not need to borrow from them; rather, they can rule over the other peoples through the success and progress they achieve, while no one rules over them.

Be compassionate toward the needy and the families who hide their need, and help them by not demanding debts, and do not forget that you are in debt to God for all the good things you own, and when you give, God gives you more, and when you forgive, God also forgives you.
Within any of thy gates: in one of your cities.
Nor shut thine hand: do not be stingy.
Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him: help him and lend to him.
God calls them to help the poor, whether by almsgiving or by lending, that is, to be merciful to the needy.
A thought in thy wicked heart: you think a wicked thought.
Thine eye be evil against thy brother: you harden your heart against him.
And he cry unto the LORD against thee: and he complains of you to God.

God warns them against wickedness and the love of money, lest they refrain from lending to the poor man when the seventh year draws near, because he will probably not be able to repay and their money will be lost to them; for if they do this, the poor man cries out to God because of their harshness, and they will be wrong in the sight of God, and He will be angry with them.
Thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him: do not be unwilling when giving.
God requires His people to lend to the poor with willing, loving hearts, and God will bless them. This confirms the importance of giving with joy.
There must be poor people among the people, and God permits this so that the love of the rich for them may show itself in helping them.

The Lord loves the cheerful giver, so the more we rejoice in doing good, the more God rejoices in us, remembering that we give to Christ in the form of the poor and that together with the poor we are members of one body, and this makes our joy in giving firm.
If one of God's people becomes poor and sells himself as a slave, he works six years only, and in the seventh year he goes out free (Ex 21).
Thy floor: the threshing floor on which the grain crops are stored.

God commands that the slave be helped from the possessions of the rich man for whom he worked when he is released in the seventh year, so he gives him of his flock, and of the grain in his storehouses, and of the juice of his winepress, such as the wine and the oil, so that this helps him to begin a new life.

The Lord reminds them that they, the masters themselves, or their fathers, were slaves in Egypt, so their releasing their slaves is an expression of their thanks to the Lord who freed them from the slavery of Egypt. By remembering this great deed that the Lord did for them, they will have compassion on their brethren. And His saying "You were bondmen in Egypt" does not mean a particular generation, that is, only the generation that came out of Egypt, but applies to all the generations of the children of Israel in every age, for what happened to their fathers is as though it happened to them, or, had the Lord not freed the fathers, the sons would have remained under slavery.

The slave may prefer not to leave his master when the time of his release comes, because he has become accustomed to him and loves him and his household and has found rest in the good treatment he received during the period of his service to his master, so he prefers to continue and remain in service. Then his master performs a certain procedure, which is boring the slave's ear (considering that the ear points to hearing and obedience), at the gate of the city, so that it is a declaration before all the people, and the slave may not complain afterward that he is forced into slavery with this master. The same procedure is carried out for the woman slave (the maidservant).

Let this matter, that is, releasing the slave free in the seventh year, not be hard on you, because the value of his service to you during the six years equals twice the wage the hired servant would have received for his work with you during this period, because the hired servant spends only the daytime working, whereas the slave works all day, day and night. If you do so and release him free, the Lord will bless you in all that you do as a reward for your obeying the commandment. For God regards the Hebrew slave as a hired servant to his brother for six years, not like slavery among the Gentiles.
May you treat those who serve you in your house gently, as your brethren, and likewise those under you at work, and not be harsh to them, remembering God's mercies toward you.

The commandment obliged the believer to sanctify to the Lord the firstling of the offspring of his animals if it was a male (of the cattle and the sheep). And since it has become the Lord's property, it is not permissible to use it in the work of the field, nor is it permissible to benefit from the wool of those animals, for the same reason. So it is offered to God, remembering that God redeemed their firstborn in Egypt, so that they were not killed with the firstborn of the Egyptians (Num 3:13).

The firstborn males are slaughtered in the house of the Lord every year and eaten by the priests, while the firstborn females or the firstborn that have a blemish are slaughtered and eaten by their owners.

Firstborn that have congenital blemishes, whether this is lameness or blindness or any other bad blemish, are not offered to the Lord (Mal 1:8). For it is fitting that the best things be offered to the King of kings, not the meanest.
And this is an indication that the animal sacrifice is nothing but a symbol of the Lamb without blemish and without defilement whose blood would be shed on the Cross.
The hart: a kind of buck.

But these firstborn that have blemishes may be eaten in the place where their owners live, that is, in their homes, just as they eat the other animals not set apart for offerings, such as gazelles and harts, and it is not necessary in this case to follow the rules of ritual purity as is the case in religious feasts.
Once again he stresses the prohibition of eating blood, whether the blood of sacrifices offered as offerings or of those eaten as ordinary food, but the blood is poured out on the ground.
Be careful to offer to God the firstfruits of your time, your money and all your abilities and talents, and you will receive from Him blessings on all that you do and live in joy.
The three main feasts
Passover: that is, passing over, and it is a memorial of the passing over of the destroying angel over the houses of God's people and his not killing their firstborn.

God reminds them to keep the Feast of the Passover in the month of Abib as a memorial of the redemption of their firstborn and their liberation from the slavery of Egypt, which symbolizes our liberation from sin by the redemption of Christ (Ex 12, 13).
The ritual of this feast includes the slaughter of sheep and cattle in the house of the Lord. The Book of Numbers

The Lord commanded that no leavened bread be eaten with the Passover meal for seven days, so nothing is eaten but unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven, as a memorial of their going out of Egypt in haste, when they had no time to leaven the dough, and it was called the bread of affliction, that is, the bread of toil, as a memorial of the hardships, difficulties and opposition from Pharaoh that they faced in going out of Egypt. This is so that the events of that day, the day of their going out of Egypt, may be before their eyes all the days of their life.
Our Church, however, offers leavened bread in the sacrament of Communion, because Christ bore our sins on the Cross, and leaven symbolizes the evil which He bore for us and redeemed us.

God commands them that there be no leavened bread with them within the borders of their lands throughout the seven days, so the Jews on the fourteenth day of the month of Abib (Nisan) at noon would remove all leaven from the houses (Ex 12:15-17), before the slaughter of the lamb between the two evenings, that is, between the afternoon and sunset (Lev 23:5). And they had to eat the whole Passover lamb on the same night, that is, the evening of the fourteenth day, which is Thursday evening, and not leave any of it until the morning of the next day. And if anything of it remained, they had to burn it with fire.
This is what our Church is careful about in the sacrament of the Eucharist, as nothing remains of the Body and Blood of the Lord after Communion.

It is not right to slaughter the Passover in any place, but it is to be in the house of the Lord, that is, in the tabernacle of meeting or Solomon's temple. The lamb is slaughtered near sunset (that is, between three in the afternoon, which is the ninth hour by Hebrew reckoning, and five in the evening, which is the eleventh hour by Hebrew reckoning, that is, around sunset.

And between the slaughtering and the cooking and then the eating, a period of time will have passed that brings us into the evening of the day, which is the time of the going out of Egypt). The Passover is eaten between the two evenings, that is, between sunset and dark, at the beginning of the fifteenth day of the month of Abib (Nisan) (Lev 23:5).

Cooking the sacrifice for eating, that is, roasting it, must be done in the house of the Lord as was mentioned before, and then everyone returns in the morning of the next day, that is, after keeping the feast of the seven days of unleavened bread, that is, they return on the twenty-second day of the month of Abib.

The Feast of Unleavened Bread is connected with the Feast of the Passover, as the Passover is eaten on the fourteenth day of Nisan in the evening, that is, the night of the fifteenth of Nisan. And since the day according to the Jewish ritual begins from the evening of the previous day after its sunset until the sunset of the following day, the eating of the Passover takes place on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread continues six more days after that, so the total days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, including the first day shared with the evening of the Passover, is seven days, from the fifteenth day until the twenty-first day.

On the last day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, that is, on the seventh day, there is a retreat, so the believer does no worldly work, and separates himself from the cares of the world and devotes the day to holding religious rites and to worship.

Take care to partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord every week, and if you have the opportunity every day do not neglect it, so that you may be nourished and filled with the greatest power in the world and enjoy divine union and rejoice in His work in you.
To put the sickle to the corn: the beginning of the harvest.

The Feast of Weeks, also called the Feast of Pentecost, falls fifty days after the beginning of the harvest, which is on the second day of the Feast of the Passover. The Feast of the Harvest is called the Feast of the Firstfruits, in which the firstfruits of the barley crop, that is, the first sheaf of barley, is offered to God (Lev 23). The Feast of the Firstfruits symbolizes the Resurrection of Christ. The Feast of Pentecost, or Weeks, is held in thanksgiving to God for the crops they harvested, and symbolizes the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, when there was a harvest and the joining of many souls to the faith.

The Lord commanded the keeping of the Feast of Weeks, rejoicing in the Lord and for the Lord. It is an agricultural feast in which the individuals of the people offer voluntary offerings according to their ability and what their means allow and the size of their crop, as the Lord gave them blessings and good things in the fruits of the land, from the crop of barley and wheat. The harvest of barley begins right after the Passover, followed by the harvest of wheat, and then comes the Feast of Pentecost.

Love feasts are held in which everyone rejoices in the blessing God has bestowed on them in the harvest of the land. The one who gives the feast includes in it the members of his household, that is, his son and daughter, his manservant and maidservant, and the Levite who lives in his city, and the stranger, the fatherless and the widow who live near him, and this takes place in the place of the house of the Lord. And in honoring the servants they remember that they were slaves in Egypt, so they have compassion on slaves and strangers.

The Christian is always joyful in the Lord's giving to him, and happy in God's grace here and then in his eternal inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven, so thank God for all His gifts so that you feel their value and your enjoyment of them increases.

The Lord commanded His people to keep the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days, ending on the eighth day with a holy convocation. This feast is the third of the great annual feasts at which every male in Israel had to appear before the Lord in the temple. During it tents were set up on the roofs of houses or in the open country as a memorial of the dwelling of the house of Israel in the wilderness and their sojourning in it, where they lived in tents and were constantly traveling. One of the features of this feast also, as in the Feast of Pentecost, was holding shared feasts in the house of the Lord. This feast was held in the seventh month (Tishri) on the fifteenth day, four days after the Day of Atonement. They also called it the Feast of Ingathering because it fell at the end of the agricultural season when they gathered the rest of the produce of the land and the fruit of the slow-bearing trees.
There is a connection between the three great feasts, as follows:
The Feast of the Passover: with the first stroke of the sickle in the harvest.
The Feast of Pentecost: when the harvest is completed.
The Feast of Tabernacles: at the end of the agricultural year and the gathering of the fruits that ripen in the late summer season.
And this feast symbolizes for us, the believers of the New Testament, our sojourning in this world and our longing to set out toward our true, lasting homeland, which is heaven.
The Book of Numbers

Here too is another new call to rejoice, for the Lord's will for them is that they rejoice and make the hearts of others rejoice with them. They are to rejoice in the gifts and blessings represented by the abundance of the crop and the multitude of fruits, and also to rejoice in giving to others, whether the consecrated, that is, the Levites, or the needy among the poor and strangers.

The Lord set the duration of the celebration at seven days. And "seven" is a number that points to completeness, and here it means complete joy. The celebration of the feast takes place in the place where the house of the Lord is, so the believer rejoices over the Lord's gifts and the blessings He has bestowed on him, and also rejoices that he gives to others of what he has.

In proportion to your love for God you are able to be a stranger to the material things of the world and to be content with little of them to meet your basic needs, and so you experience the work of God in you and rejoice, indeed you are able to make those around you happy.

God commands the attendance of all the males of His people at the three feasts mentioned above. What is meant by the Feast of Unleavened Bread is the two feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread, for their time is the same. The male represents the whole family, for he is a delegate for the females. The attendance of the males has spiritual purposes, which are:
1- Strengthening their faith in the one God and in worshiping Him in His holy temple.
2- Strengthening unity among all the tribes.
3- Encouraging them spiritually by offering one worship together.
4- Giving gifts to the needy, so that they do not come to these feasts without offerings to God of which the needy eat.
Each one gives of the offerings and gifts as much as his ability allows and according to his standing and in proportion to the Lord's blessing with which He has blessed him.

Remember that you will stand before God on the day of judgment, so do not stand before Him empty, but let there be acts of worship and works of goodness for you to present before Him, with all that you have endured for His sake, so that you may have a share with Him in heaven.

entries.section: (5) Justice and keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Officers: leaders, agents of authority, local heads.

Moses commands them to appoint judges and officers for themselves in all their cities when they settle in the Promised Land, so that they may judge with justice in the disputes and problems among people, and so that they may live in safety and peace.

entries.section: (5) Justice and keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: God set for Moses three strict principles for judgment:
1- Thou shalt not wrest judgment: that is, do not deviate in your judgment in favor of one party at the expense of the other.

2- Thou shalt not respect persons: that is, do not take into account, when judging, the persons of the disputants; everyone is equal before the law, so there is no flattery of the rich or the notable and no pity for the guilty among the poor.

3- Neither take a gift: Moses made clear that the reason for the prohibition of taking a bribe is that it blinds the eyes of the wise, that is, it makes the sensible close their eyes to the truth and so they issue false judgments. Likewise the Book of Numbers showed them that bribery perverts the words of the righteous, for it is tempting and affects judges even if they are honorable, and makes them utter words contrary to what they know in their hearts to be the truth.

entries.section: (5) Justice and keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The repetition of the word justice here is to stress the necessity of following the truth and keeping away from injustice in judgments. And he promised them that if they follow justice in their judgments they will live, that is, their existence as a nation will continue and they will live a safe, settled life and ensure that they deserve to remain in the land the Lord gave them, so that He does not drive them out of it as a recompense for disobedience and injustice.

entries.section: (5) Justice and keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The grove: a pillar set up on high places (it may be of wood or other material) or a tree planted beside the pagan altar.

The Lord forbids the manifestations of pagan worship that existed in the region, so that His people may not imitate what the other peoples do; the Lord commands them not to set up pillars or plant trees beside the altar they build for the Lord.

entries.section: (5) Justice and keeping away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The image: a pillar of stones.

Likewise they are not to set up stone pillars for the same purpose, so that they do not imitate the pagans in their worship and superstitions and do not practice their rites and so fall into the same errors, because the Lord hates such works and practices and is angry with those who practice them.

Do not rush to judge anyone, lest you err unintentionally. And before you pass a judgment, seek God to receive His guidance and to feel that you are in His presence, so that you will be just in your judgments.
The counsel of the priest, laws for the king, and the worship of idols

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: In the following verses he speaks about the punishment for the worship of idols. And in this verse he directs them to offer sound worship to God by sacrificing an animal without blemish, out of respect and love for God, and because it is a type of Christ, the Lamb without blemish.

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Transgresseth his covenant: betrays God's covenant.
The host of heaven: the planets and the stars.
If anyone of God's people dares to betray Him by worshiping idols, whether the planets or the stars or any strange gods, he deserves a great punishment.

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: God stresses the necessity of examining the one who has turned away from His worship to the worship of idols and of making certain of this deed.

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: If the conviction is established, the Lord specifies the sentence that must be applied to the apostate, whether a man or a woman, which is death by stoning. This sentence is carried out at the gates of the city so that it is in the sight of all, and the others see it and take warning.

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The Lord stresses the necessity of not being hasty, so that the sentence may not be unjust. And He requires that it be supported by the testimony of witnesses, two or at least three, to avoid any doubt about the soundness of the sentence that is issued. The testimony of one witness is not enough to make sure that the accusation is true, and so that there may be no suspicion of bias by one person against another, resorting to spite against him by fabricating this accusation.

entries.section: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: The witnesses begin by stoning the one who worshiped idols, because they are responsible for their testimony, for if he is innocent they bear his guilt before God. Then the rest of the people stone him after them until he dies, and so they put away evil from the midst of the people.

Although God is longsuffering toward us now, our worship of other gods besides Him, such as money, pride and the lusts of the world, deserves death. If we fall, we must repent quickly and strive to return from this apostasy to the worship of God and love for Him.

entries.section: (2) Consulting the priest and the judge

paragraphs.text: Between blood and blood: a murder case between the one killed and the killer.
Between plea and plea: a dispute between two parties.
Between stroke and stroke: between the one wronged and the aggressor, who could wound himself to appear to be the one wronged.

If it is difficult for the local judges in one of the cities of the people of Canaan to decide in some disputes, the problem is referred to a higher judicial body in the large cities. There was a judicial body in the villages and small towns made up of three judges, while in the large cities it was made up of twenty-three judges, and if the matter was too difficult for this higher judicial body it was referred to the highest judicial body, the Sanhedrin, made up of the priests and judges in the city where the house of the Lord is. In all cases the party with the problem is bound to obey the judicial rulings that are issued according to God's Law.

entries.section: (2) Consulting the priest and the judge

paragraphs.text: Whoever violates the judicial rulings is considered a rebel against God and His Law and must be put to death, and then all the people fear and submit to God's Law and judgment.

Christ calls us to resort to the priests to resolve problems (Mt 18:17), and likewise St. Paul the Apostle (1 Cor 6:2). May we consult our fathers the priests and their assistants among the wise servants to solve our problems from their beginning, so that we live in peace and do not need to resort to the courts and all the disturbances they cause.

After the people settle in the land of Canaan, they may think of setting up a king for themselves like the rest of the peoples around them and as they saw in Egypt. Although this matter angers God because He is their King, His love for them and His longsuffering led Him to give them conditions for setting up this king, which are:
1- That they pray that God would guide them to the suitable king.
2- That he not be a foreigner, lest he lead them to the worship of idols.
He completes the conditions for choosing the king, saying:

3- That he not multiply horses, which were reckoned the greatest military force at that time, lest he become proud and depend on his own strength and not on God, and lest he enter needlessly into wars with those around him, all of which is a burden on his people and at the expense of their material needs and their comfort.

4- That he not resort to Egypt, which was the first empire in the world and the dominant one at that time and remained strong even after the rise of empires after it, in order to acquire more horses from it or to ally himself with it, and so not trust in God, and perhaps become tied to the worship of idols.

5- That he not be preoccupied with his lusts, marrying many women who distract him from God and from leading the people, and who may turn his heart to the worship of idols if they are foreigners, as happened with King Solomon (1 Kgs 11:
6- That he not be preoccupied with wealth, acquiring silver and gold, which would distract him from God and burden his people and make them poor, so that he falls into greed and pride.

The seventh condition is that the king write for himself a copy of the Law that the priests have, to read in it always and lead the people according to it, and carry it out, so that he protects himself from pride and prolongs his days in the kingdom, and the people love to have his sons succeed him because they are from him. Godly kings appeared who cared for God's Law and submitted to it, such as David, Hezekiah and Josiah (1 Kgs 11:13, 1 Kgs 16:20, 1 Kgs 21, 22).
May you take care to read the Holy Bible and carry out its commandments every day, and so protect yourself from many sins and enjoy fellowship with God.
The share of the priests, keeping away from pagan practices, and the prophets

entries.section: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: God stresses that the priests and the whole tribe of Levi do not own land in Canaan but devote themselves to the service of God and eat of God's portion, that is, the sacrifices and offerings presented to the house of the Lord; that is, their share is the Lord's share of the offerings.

entries.section: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Here he mentions the share of the priests from the sacrifices that the people offer to God, and it includes these parts:

1- The shoulder: it is the right foreleg, which is called the heave shoulder (Ex 29:27, 28, Lev 7:30-34). It signifies the striving of the priest, his walking in the way of God, and his help and care for the people.

2- The two cheeks: they are part of the head, and it is noticed that they are not mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus, perhaps because of their small value, and it was known that they belonged to the priest's share. They signify the priest's speech and teaching.
3- The maw: it means the intestines, and it also is not mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus for the same reason given for the cheeks. It signifies meeting the priest's material needs.

4- The wave breast: it is mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus and not mentioned here, perhaps because it was well known that it belonged to the priest's share, and it is the most important part of the sacrifice.

entries.section: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: In addition to the priest's share of the sacrifices, he has also a share in the agricultural crops. He had the firstfruits of the wheat, the grape juice and the oil, and also the wool that is shorn from the sheep.

entries.section: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: The reason for these privileges granted to the priest is, as stated in (v. 1), that he has no land or livestock like the rest of the people to provide him with such needs; its reason is also what is stated here, that he is consecrated to stand in prayer before the Lord in His holy house to perform the ritual and spiritual services, he and his descendants after him, so his material needs must be provided for.

entries.section: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: It may happen that some Levites have a genuine desire of the heart to devote themselves to the service of the house of the Lord, outside their turn, and so they leave their cities of residence, which are considered a sojourn for them, because they had no share in the land but their cities were given to them by the rest of the tribes, and they come to the house of the Lord and serve there with the rest of their Levite brethren who are on duty; in this case they are also given a full share of the tithes, offerings and other things, in addition to their right to any other source of income from what they inherited from their fathers.

God cares for His consecrated servants and provides for their needs because He is a tender Father who cares for His children, so rely on Him, confident of His love for you, and fear no troubles in the future, for He is with you, ordering your affairs, defending you and protecting you from every evil.
Abomination: filth, a vile act and the work of Satan.
He warns them, after they dwell in the land of Canaan, not to imitate the pagans around them in their worship of strange gods, for this is rebellion and betrayal of God.
He mentions here examples of the forbidden pagan practices, which are:
1- Human sacrifices: He forbids them to offer their children to be burned with fire or to roast them on the bronze heated with fire, which is the image of the god Molech.
2- Divination: claiming to know the unseen, whether by interpreting dreams, the stars or the palm of the hand ...
3- Augury: it means taking omens of good fortune and of ill fortune.
4- Optimism (taking omens for good).
5- Witchcraft: using the power of Satan to carry out a benefit or ward off harm or hurt others by using spells and riddles.
6- One who charms with a charm: presenting requests to the gods with incense.
7- One who asks a jinn or a familiar spirit: these are kinds of demons, and they thought that there are spirits that attend upon human beings, so they ask for their help.
8- One who consults the dead: that is, summoning spirits, which is calling up demons who pretend to be the spirits of the dead.

The Lord wants us to depend on Him alone, so everyone who practices these deeds is an abomination to Him, because they mean relying on satanic powers that do not want good for the children of men and draw them toward disobedience against God. Therefore it was one of the reasons for which the Lord drove the Canaanites out of the land.

God asks His children, whether in the Old Testament or in the New Testament, to be perfect. And these defiled deeds deprive the believers of the perfection that the Lord commanded them to seek, as in (Gen 17:1), (Mt 5:48), for they lower the dignity of man and his divine image, since he seeks the help of the enemy of humanity, the enemy of good, ignoring Almighty God.
Succeed them: take their place.

It is not strange that the pagan peoples resort to such defiled deeds, for they believe in vanities because of their inability to perceive the existence of the true God, therefore God permits His people to take their place in the land from which He drives them out. But as for them, they are a royal race, a holy nation and a chosen people; these foolish, defiled deeds are not fitting for them and the Lord does not allow them.

Do not let your heart be attached to knowing the unseen or be dazzled by the works of demons, even if they hide behind repeating prayers from the Holy Bible, but seek the Lord your God, and He will guide you and deliver you and keep you from these satanic works and solve your problems, so that you do not lower yourself and abase yourself to Satan your enemy.

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: After the Lord forbade resorting to magic and the knowledge of the unseen and condemned their practice, He promised His people that He would raise up a series of prophets whom they would ask and listen to, not false prophets but those sent from the Lord. And these prophets the Lord chooses from within their tribes, that is, from the sons of Jacob, and not strangers. And they will be like Moses, that is, with the same spirit of care that Moses showed toward his people, and they will continue his work. This divine promise was fulfilled later more completely in the person of the Lord Jesus Christ, who took the office of prophet (He is priest, king and prophet), as He spoke to the people with the words of eternal life, declaring that He does not speak of Himself but speaks what the Father gives Him (Jn 5:45, 46; Acts 3:21-26; Acts 7:37). So this verse is a prophecy of the Incarnation of Christ, and Moses is a type of Christ, and there is a likeness between them, but within limits, because Christ is God (see the commentary on Heb 3 in Part Five of the Encyclopedia).

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: He reminds them of what they asked when they were at Mount Horeb (Ex 20), when they were afraid of the awesome manifestations that surrounded their seeing the glory of the Lord when He gave them the Ten Commandments. They asked that Moses be a mediator between them and the Lord, so that they would no longer be terrified and lest they die. And the Lord approved their words and answered them.

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: God alone is the One who raises up the prophets and puts His words in their mouths. (And every prophet afterward would say, "Thus saith the LORD.") And the Lord repeats that the prophets will be from the sons of Jacob and not from foreigners.

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: The person who does not listen to the word of the Lord from the mouth of His prophets and act on it, the Lord will call him to account and judge him. For the Lord requires them to obey His words that come from the mouth of His prophets.

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: A new warning against the false prophets who dare to speak against the Lord, saying words that did not come from Him, claiming that they are divine revelation, and likewise the one who calls to false gods, claiming that he is conveying from them, drawing people to worship them. Such a person is put to death because he leads the people astray.

entries.section: (3) The true and the false prophets

paragraphs.text: The people may be perplexed before the words of the prophets and unable to judge whether they are truthful or false. Therefore the Lord gave a sign by which they can distinguish between the true prophet and the false prophet, which is: if the things that the prophet prophesied actually happen, his prophecy was true and he spoke on behalf of the Lord, but if they do not happen, this means that he is a false prophet who dared against God and claimed prophecy and conveyed from the Lord words He did not say, so he utters thoughts of his own and not from the inspiration of God.

Pay attention to God's word that He sends to you through the mouth of those around you, the priests and teachers, to guide you in the way of your life, and do not be led by the word of the world, however dazzling, for it is false and leads you astray, and in this way you keep your life in tranquility and peace.
Cities of refuge and false witness

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: Cutteth off: destroyed and drove out.

God commands them, after the pagans, the original inhabitants of the land, are driven out and they dwell in their place in the land of Canaan, to set apart three cities to which the unintentional killer may flee. Note that Moses had set apart three cities east of the Jordan for refuge, other than these three which he wants to set apart west of the Jordan (Num 35:

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: He must repair and prepare the roads that lead to those cities so that it is easy for the fleeing killer to run and take refuge in them. They must also divide their land, which the Lord gives them as a portion, into three parts, and it was divided lengthwise from south to north, and in the middle of each part a city of refuge, which is matched east of the Jordan by another city of refuge, so that they have six cities of refuge.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: He mentions here one of the rulings concerning unintentional killing, and gives an example of it: one who struck his neighbor without intending to kill him, and there was no enmity or quarrel between them before (Num 35:

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: And he gives here a second example of the possibility of killing without intent, which is two persons going to the forest to cut trees; while one of them strikes the trunk of a tree with the axe in order to cut it, the iron part of the axe head slips from the wooden handle and flies far away and strikes his companion and kills him. In this case the killer must flee immediately to the nearest of the three cities set apart for this purpose, to escape being taken in revenge.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: The avenger of blood: the nearest relative of the person killed, who wants to take vengeance for him on the killer.

The unintentional killer must flee quickly to the cities of refuge so that the relative of the one killed, who wants to take revenge for him, does not overtake him when his anger is intense at the killing of his relative, and catch up with him before he reaches the city of refuge and kill him, whereas the Law does not allow that, because the killing of his neighbor was not out of spite or enmity or premeditation, but happened by accident and against his will.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: So that this may happen, that is, so that the relative of the one killed may not overtake the killer, the Lord commanded them to designate the three cities as cities of refuge, and no one is allowed to kill the killer who reaches one of them (map 9).

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: If the land they possess becomes wide, as the Lord God promised their fathers, so as to include all the lands promised to the fathers (and this depends on their keeping the covenant and their walking according to the commandments and judgments of the Law that God gave them), they must designate three other new cities so that the number of cities of refuge may match the width of the land. Thus they would have nine cities of refuge, but they did not keep God's Law completely, so they did not expand except in the days of David and Solomon, and in the days of these two kings they possessed places but there were no Jews in them, so they did not need the other three cities and were content with the first six set apart for refuge.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: The Lord made clear that the reason for adding three new cities is that the distance of any city of refuge from all the cities of Israel should be suitable for the one taking refuge in it to reach it in a suitable time, that is, within one day, before the one who wants to take vengeance overtakes him, so that the responsibility for shedding innocent blood would fall on the whole people.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: In the case of intentional killing, that is, where one person hates another and lies in wait for him and kills him, even if he flees to the cities of refuge the elders of his city bring him from there and the relative of the victim kills him, that is, carries out on him God's sentence of death. But in the New Testament revenge is not permitted and the killer is punished according to the criminal law and the priests help him to repent, so he receives forgiveness of his sins, and even if he is executed he has a place in heaven.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: He warns them against leniency toward the intentional killer, for he must be punished so that the rest of the people may fear because of the gravity of the sin of murder and show their respect for the life of the one killed, that is, his blood that was shed on the ground.

God's tenderness makes Him preserve your life even if you are in the wrong. So thank Him and ask Him to cover you and forgive you your sins, and you also be one who seeks excuses for those around you who go wrong.

entries.section: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: The landmark: the boundary of the land, which was marked by stones or pieces of iron or trees or by ditches.

The Lord forbids the owner of the land to try to enlarge the area of the land he owns at the expense of cutting off a part of his neighbor's lands and annexing it to his own lands, for this is considered a usurpation of the rights of others and an assault on private property. The Lord arranged the way in which the land is distributed to the tribes, families and persons, and departing from this arrangement means making light of the Lord's work and is sometimes a cause of the anger of the wronged owner of the land, who rises up and kills the one who usurped his land.
Do not wrong another and usurp his rights. And on the other hand, hold fast to your faith and your rites and do not be lax in them or allow anyone to draw you away from them.

The Lord always requires them to investigate and examine cases well before issuing sentences of condemnation. In (ch. 17), when He spoke to them about the punishment of one who worships other gods, He specified the necessity of two or at least three witnesses to testify against him. The same warning against haste and lack of care in judgment He repeats here concerning one who commits some offense or sin, for it requires two or three witnesses to decide the sentence of condemnation, as He also mentioned in (Num 35:30).
Testifying wrongfully: swerving away from the truth in his testimony.

Here is the ruling on violating the ninth commandment, which was mentioned among the Ten Commandments in (Ex 20:16), which is "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour." If someone bears false witness against another in order to harm him, the matter is decided as will come in the following verses.

Here God sets a system so that no one thinks of taking revenge for himself by himself, which would make matters unstable and cause chaos in people's dealings with one another. He set up a judicial system (ch. 17:8-10) made up of the priests and the judges, and made two levels of judgment, a local level and a central level; so if someone accuses another of a false charge, they appear before the judges.

The judges must examine the matter well and be careful, lest they issue unjust sentences. So if it becomes clear to them, after examination and investigation, that the witness accused his companion wrongly and that he is lying in what he said against him, then the same sentence is applied to the witness that the charge he brought against his brother would have required and which would have been applied to his brother had it been true; thus he is punished with the same punishment that he wanted to inflict on his neighbor.
The purpose of punishing the false witness is that others may fear and keep away from false witness.

He warns them against leniency in punishing the false witness. Whoever testifies against another on a charge whose penalty is death is put to death in his place, and if the penalty is the plucking out of an eye, the breaking of a tooth, or the cutting off of a hand or foot, the false witness is punished with the same penalty.
What a person does returns upon him. Therefore let us set the Lord and His fear before us at all times, because we shall suffer the result of what we do.
The law of war

The people were about to enter into battles with the inhabitants of the Promised Land. Those nations possessed a great deal of military equipment, including horses and chariots, while the army of Israel had none of it; they were infantry only. Therefore the Lord commanded them not to fear the strength of the enemies and their equipment, and reminded them that, just as He had been with them and brought them out of the land of Egypt, delivering them from Pharaoh and his army, so He is still with them, fighting for them in their holy wars.

Before entering any war, the people had to listen to their priests, to whom the Lord had entrusted a role in preparing for war. For example, the priest was to encourage the people, remind them of the Lord's promises, bless them, pray to God to give them victory, and offer burnt offerings and peace offerings (1 Sam 13:9).

The priest says to them: you are now ready for war against your enemies, so be strong and take courage, do not be fainthearted before the enemy, and let no doubt of victory trouble your hearts. However well armed the enemy may be, do not fear them and do not dread their violence.
And he tells them the reason for this confidence and strong faith in victory over the enemy: that the Lord goes before them and fights for them, and it is He who will give them the victory.
Do not fear the wars of the devil or the threats of any man, for God is with you. Hold fast to Him and ask for the intercession of the saints, and you will be victorious in all your wars.

entries.section: (2) Exemption of certain groups from war

paragraphs.text: The officers: the leaders of the people.
The following groups are exempted from war:
1- One who has built a house and has not dedicated it and rejoiced in it, so that he does not enter the war sorrowful and fight without strength.
2- One who has planted a vineyard and has not eaten of its fruit.
3- One who has betrothed a wife and has not married her and rejoiced in her.
4- The fearful.
It is noted that these exemptions were for the following reasons:
1- The human feelings of one who has acquired something new, or is bound in an emotional relationship, or is overcome by fear.
2- Presenting men who are full of zeal and strength, not sorrowful or preoccupied with material matters, or fighting against fear, which would hinder them from victory.
3- If the number of men is small, the rest believe that victory comes through God and not through numbers, as happened with Gideon (Judg 7:7).

entries.section: (2) Exemption of certain groups from war

paragraphs.text: After those exempted from war are sent away, the officers are appointed as leaders of the soldiers to lead them in the war.
