The basket is the vessel in which the fruits are gathered, so blessing it means blessing what is inside it, so that the harvest is abundant.
And the kneading trough is the vessel in which the flour is kneaded and becomes bread, so blessing it means abundance of good and satisfaction.

"Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out" means that you will be blessed in your works and in all that you strive for, because carrying out these works requires going out and coming in, so this means that the blessing includes all the activities of life.

The Lord gives you victory over everyone who is hostile to you or resists you. If they attack you in great numbers with their soldiers drawn up in ranks and massed against you, that is, coming by one road, He scatters them before you, so that they flee by many roads.
Do not be disturbed by the wars of the demons, but take refuge in God by prayer and all the means of grace, and the demons will fear you and flee.

The Lord blesses the storehouses of your harvests, so that they are filled with an abundance of good things, and you succeed in all the works you undertake (as was said in the Book of Genesis about Joseph the son of Jacob, "that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand," Gen 39:3). And the blessing in the land that the Lord gives you means settling in the Promised Land and not being exposed to any outside threat.

The Lord raises you to a high rank among the peoples, so that you are a holy people, attributed to Him and His own. That is if you keep His commandments and act according to His laws, and then the other peoples will fear you.

A repetition of what came in v. 4. The Lord affirms to them a second time that He will bless their offspring and the offspring of their animals and the harvests of their land and the fruits of their trees.

God's heavenly treasures are the rains that give abundant harvests to His people, so that they become richer than the peoples around them, and these peoples come to borrow from them, while the people of God borrow from no one because of the abundance of good things they have.
And if you listen to the commandments of the Lord you will be superior to all peoples in growth and prosperity, and you will not be at their rear but always lifted above them.
The condition for obtaining all these blessings is holding fast to the commandments of God and keeping away from the worship of idols.

The cause of all the curses, whether those mentioned here or those mentioned in the previous chapter, is disobedience to the word of God. And these curses are discipline to bring man back to God by repentance.
This curse is the opposite of the blessing mentioned in (v. 3), so that failure pursues the person, whether he lives in the city or the village, that is, in all his works.

And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 5): instead of the blessing that increases your fruits to fill the basket, and the abundant flour that fills the kneading trough, scarcity and small harvest prevail instead of abundance and satisfaction.

And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 4): there will be no blessing in your offspring or in the young of your cattle and sheep, and the blessing is removed from the harvests of your land, so that good things are fewer and you are in want and distress.

And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 6): instead of the Lord's blessing your works, you fail in everything you strive for, and failure and disappointment follow you wherever you go and in any place where you settle.
Rebuke: reproach and violent reproof.

They lose their peace and are troubled throughout their lives, and God is angry with them, in addition to the reproach of people, and this trouble continues until their lives quickly end because of the multitude of their sins.
The Lord strikes them with epidemics that spread among them and keep hold of them until they destroy most of them, so that their name is blotted out from the land that He gives them.
The Lord lists for them the diseases that will seize them to destroy them, which are:
Consumption: a disease that affects the lung in man and destroys it, and it is highly contagious.
Fever: it is of many kinds, and among its common symptoms is a very high body temperature. Chills: the severe shivering resulting from infection with certain fevers.
Inflammation: it affects many systems of the body such as the nerves and muscles, and many diseases result from it, such as rheumatism and others.
Drought: the scarcity of water necessary for the needs of man, animals, and crops. In man and animals it may cause death, and in crops it causes withering and the ruin of the harvests.
Scorching: the intense heat brought by the hot wind, which may cause the death of people and the ruin of crops and fruits.
Withering: severe weakness, the decline of bodily strength, and the loss of activity and vitality.

A rhetorical image portraying the scorching heat as if the sky had become bronze, which strongly reflects the sun's heat and gives no opening for rain to lessen the intensity of the heat, and as if the earth had become iron, unfit for the sprouting of any seeds, so that it is as if nature had turned against man in answer to man's turning against God.
Instead of the rains that water the crops, the winds carry dust that destroys them and makes the air suffocating until man perishes.

And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 7): instead of victory over the enemies, defeat overtakes you and your army is scattered into dispersed bands seeking an outlet to flee from the enemies in search of safety, and they are scattered in many kingdoms in which they feel no reassurance but are always anxious and troubled.

And because of the multitude of those slain in war and of the dead from epidemics and diseases, their bodies lie scattered on the ground with no one to bury them, and the birds of prey and the beasts tear at them, with no one to drive them off or chase them away, because the remnant that is left are occupied with their worries and sorrows and the affliction that surrounds them.
Here the Lord adds another group of diseases that strike them as a result of their turning away from Him, which are chronic and dangerous diseases that resist healing, and they are:

The boil (the boil of Egypt): the boil is pustules, festering sores, and abscesses. It was ascribed to Egypt because it was one of the ten plagues (the sixth plague) with which the Lord struck the Egyptians in the days of Moses, for their preventing the people of God from leaving Egypt (Ex 9:10). Hemorrhoids: a painful disease that affects the area of excretion in man.
The scab: a skin rash that disfigures the skin and makes people shun the sufferer.
The itch: scratching, which causes pain and distress to the one afflicted with it.

As a result of the multitude of calamities that surround them and their bewilderment at what happens to them, they are struck with madness and their behavior is marked by recklessness and instability, and they may also be struck with blindness as a result of the air being saturated with germs from the polluted dust, and not only bodily blindness but blindness of mind and spirit, so that they do not know how to act toward what faces them, and they live bewildered, lost in thought and will.

They become unable to see in broad daylight, that is, as a result of their confusion and bewilderment, so they stray from the right way to overcome their problems even if the way to do so is clear and evident, but walk in various ways that lead them to failure and frustration, and enemies gain mastery over them, so that they are only defeated, humiliated, and oppressed, finding no one to lend them a hand of help, neither from people nor from God, because the Lord their Savior hides His face from them for their sins and their lack of repentance.
Here is a description of the manifestations of the persecution that the people will suffer from the enemies, which are:
1- The enemy who has conquered you invades you, and the wife whom you betrothed he takes for himself.
2- The house that you build to live in, the enemy seizes, and he dwells in it and deprives you of it.
3- The vineyard that you planted, you do not enjoy its fruit, for the enemy plunders it and you take nothing from it.

The enemy also seizes your livestock and your oxen and slaughters them before your eyes, and they give you nothing of what they slaughter. They take your donkey by force in your presence and you cannot do anything to recover it from them; they drive off your sheep and take them as spoil for themselves and you cannot resist them.

Your sons and daughters become captives of the enemies, and they take them into captivity under your sight, and you see them as they take them away, and you grieve with the utmost sorrow at what you see, and you have nothing but weeping until your eyes are weary and grief overtakes you over the loss of the children, without its being possible for you to do anything to rescue them from the hands of the enemies.

The crops of your plantings and all that you toiled for of the produce of your lands and the work of your hands are enjoyed by others, of the peoples who have conquered you, with whom you had no connection or acquaintance before, and you become broken and crushed all the days of your life.

What will befall you of calamities, and what your eyes will behold of the manifestations of oppression and humiliation of you and your sons, will make your mind fly away, so that you become like a madman who stumbles in his thoughts and has no control over himself.

And this is another blow of diseases in addition to what was mentioned earlier in (v. 22). For the Lord permits severe sores to afflict their knees and legs which they cannot be healed of, spreading over all parts of their bodies, so that it is hard for them to sit, stand, or walk, and any bodily activity becomes impossible for them.

You go into captivity and are subject to another people with whom neither you nor your fathers had any connection before, who force you to practice their pagan worship, so that you bow down to their gods made by hands, which are nothing but wood and stone, and even your king and your leaders become weak and are taken into captivity. This happened in the Assyrian captivity of the kingdom of Israel and then the Babylonian captivity of the kingdom of Judah.

Because of the severity of the horrors that befall you, the peoples look at you with astonishment and amazement at the humiliation you have come to, after the loftiness, exaltation, and high standing you had among the nations. And you will be the example pointed to when speaking of the utmost degrees of humiliation and degradation, and even the peoples to whom you are captive will mock you and ridicule you.
In spite of your toil and the great effort you expend in cultivating your fields, you will not reap harvests from them, because the Lord will send locusts upon you to eat them.
Likewise with the vines you plant, you will not gather their fruit nor drink of their wine, because the Lord will send worms upon you to eat them.

And with all the olive trees you have throughout your land, you will not be able to use any of their oil, because pests and diseases will strike the fruit before it ripens, and it will be scattered, spoiled, and fall to the ground.
Even your sons and daughters, you will not rejoice in having them at your side, for you will be deprived of them, because the enemy will take them captive to his country far from you.
The cricket ("locust"): the field cricket and kinds of insects that spoil plants, so that they attack the crops and ruin them and nothing of them is harvested.

After the strangers in your land were subject to your legislation and judgments, and even served you in many works of farming, drawing water, cutting wood, and tending cattle and sheep, they become the masters and rule over you, and you are brought low and become of lesser standing than those whose masters you formerly were.

And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 12). After they enjoyed material abundance, so that they lent to the peoples around them, the matter is reversed and, because of their extreme poverty, they become in need of begging from others, reaching the lowest degrees of humiliation and shame. And the strangers become the masters while the people of Israel become subject to them.

Do not be drawn to the pleasure of sin, lest its evil consequences come upon you and God be angry with you, and you lose the blessings you enjoy and lose your peace and your eternity, and instead be in great trouble and humiliation.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: The cause of all these previous curses is disobedience to the word of God, and these curses continue until they destroy man.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: The calamities that befall you will be a lesson and a warning to later generations and a sign of the severity of the Lord's anger at your disobedience, and an affirmation of His authority, able to raise the one who does righteousness and punish the wicked. Indeed, the later generations will suffer from the inheritance of the painful state into which they were born or in which they grew up.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: All the curses that strike them are the result of their not having been glad in the worship of the Lord and not having come to apply His commandments except under compulsion and with strain, despite the gifts the Lord had bestowed on them which made them rich, for instead of thanking Him for them, they were occupied by them away from Him and from their duties toward Him and their worship of Him.

It is truly sad that when a person's blessings and good things multiply, he is often occupied by them from his duties toward his Creator, so that all his thought is confined to how to keep them, increase them, and enjoy them at the expense of his fellowship with God. And instead of remembering God as the true giver of these blessings, his heart and mind are occupied with the material he possesses. May we never forget that all the successes we achieve in the various fields are from God's kindnesses to us, so that this increases our attachment to the Lord and we increase our thanks to Him for all His gifts.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: Beginning with this verse and up to (v. 57), the Lord lists for them the troubles that the enemies will cause them if the Lord abandons them because of their turning away from His worship. The people then return to the bitter bondage they endured before, for the Lord hands them over to their enemies and they enslave and humiliate them. And instead of the abundance they enjoy in the Promised Land, they suffer hunger, nakedness, and need even of the necessities of life.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: The Lord uses these enemies to discipline His people, so they come from distant places (as happened with the Babylonians, the Assyrians, the Persians, the Seleucids, and then the Romans) and swoop down on them with speed and ferocity as the eagle does when it swoops on its prey, and they are foreign nations whose language they do not know.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: These enemies are hard of heart, so they respect no elder and have no pity on the young, but are violent and destroy everyone.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: The invading peoples seize all the good things of the land, eating what the animals bear and what ripens of the fruits of the land, so that nothing is left to them of wheat, wine, oil, or the offspring of animals, and they suffer hunger and are exposed to death.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: A siege is laid on all their cities until the fortresses, strongholds, and walls collapse, which they had been confident would be secure and protect them from the invaders. No city of theirs will be spared this siege, and they fall into the hands of their enemies.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: As a result of the severity of the siege they are unable to provide the minimum of necessary food, so famines spread and hunger grows so intense that people lose the feeling of any lofty human emotions such as the emotion of fatherhood and motherhood, and they slaughter their sons to eat their flesh (2 Kgs 6:24-30).

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: When the enemies besiege the cities of the people of God and they are near to dying of hunger, the man who lives in luxury slaughters one of his sons to eat his flesh and begrudges his wife and the rest of his sons giving them any of the flesh of the slaughtered son. Thus their condition reaches this humiliation and hardness of heart.

entries.section: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

paragraphs.text: The afterbirth ("placenta"): a part connected to the fetus that carries nourishment from the mother to the fetus and comes out with the newborn at birth, and is called in colloquial speech "al-khalas."

And also the woman who lives in such luxury that she would not set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicacy, that is, she lived in complete ease that did not require her to do any work, she too, when her hunger grows intense in the siege, is forced to eat the afterbirth that comes out in childbirth, and is also forced to slaughter her children and cook them, and does not agree that anyone share with her in eating them, not even her husband or her other children whom she has not yet slaughtered.
He affirms here that disobedience to the word of God and disrespect for His name bring many curses and plagues upon His people, and deadly diseases.
Diseases: plural of disease, that is, sickness.

The Lord returns once more and strikes them with every disease with which He had struck the Egyptians when He punished Pharaoh and his people. So there strike them the diseases and epidemics at which the people of God were terrified and afraid when they saw them afflict the Egyptians; these diseases will cling to them and be incurable.

The Lord makes them fall prey to many diseases, not only those written in this book but also many other diseases that are not mentioned here, which do their work in their bodies until they die from the horror and ravage of those diseases upon them.

The Lord's promise to their fathers to multiply their offspring was conditional on their keeping the covenant. Since they violated His commandments, He turns back and removes His blessing from them, so that they become a few men again and a nation small in number as they were before.
As the Lord's blessing was great for His people, so also His plagues will be great to destroy them.
And because of God's anger at them, He scatters them in the lands of the world, so that they live among the pagans who force them to worship idols made of stone and wood.
There shall be no rest for the sole of your foot: you shall have no settled place.
Failing of eyes: weakness of sight.
Sorrow of mind ("languishing of soul"): depression.

In your stay among the invading nations you will feel no rest, reassurance, or stability, but your eyesight will weaken from much weeping and lamenting over the way your circumstances have gone, and you will find no pleasure in the delights of life, for depression and distress will possess you as a result of the calamities and sorrows.
And you will be threatened with death at any moment, so you will live in fear and terror, not safe for your lives, neither by day nor by night.

You will not feel rest at any moment of your life, whether by day or by night. For from the many dangers and diseases you endure during the day, you will wish that the day would pass quickly so that night comes, thinking that it will give you rest, but the opposite happens, for the night brings new calamities and woes, and you will go back and wish that it would pass so that the day may come and be better, but sadly your whole life will become misery.

Finally Israel will find itself once again subject to the humiliation of bondage in Egypt after the Lord brought them out of it by the hand of Moses, saying to them that they would not return to bondage again, but this promise was conditional on their obedience to the commandment, which they did not keep. So this is a warning of their return to bondage and that they will be carried to Egypt in ships as captives, where they will be offered for sale as slaves and people from the other nations will not come forward to buy them, because they are not suitable in their view as slaves, for their leanness and weakness from the diseases and troubles they endured.
This is a terrible picture of the height of what they will suffer of pains and troubles that are hard to describe.

And this happened when Egypt attacked the land of the Jews and captured King Jehoahaz, and also when the Jews fled to Egypt at the Babylonian invasion and the destruction of Jerusalem, and at the attack of Titus the Roman in the year 70 AD and his killing of the Jews, some of them were sent to Egypt.

Persevere in your striving against sin, and you will enjoy God's help and fellowship and then the Kingdom of Heaven; this striving is restful and attractive, whereas the pains resulting from sin are beyond endurance and their result is perdition in eternal torment.
The covenant of the Lord

Moses reminded the people of the ten plagues with which God struck Pharaoh in order to deliver them from his bondage. Some of them had seen these plagues as children, and others had certainly heard of them from their fathers.

Moses grieves over the people's lack of faith in God's power and their lack of submission to Him, for they refused to enter the Promised Land and wandered in the wilderness forty years until those who refused had died.

God wants to reveal His wisdom to you and guide you in all your ways, if you love Him, give yourself to prayer and the reading of the Holy Bible, and remain steadfast in His Church. Do not neglect Him, lest He abandon you and you lose your sensitivity and understanding.

God worked a miracle for them in His care for them in the wilderness, for He preserved their clothes and their sandals for forty years. It is not natural for clothes or sandals to last so long, but it was the blessing of God (ch. 8:4).

Throughout the time of wandering in the wilderness they did not eat bread, which is the basic food necessary for bodily life, and they did not drink wine, which they think strengthens the body. Rather, their food was limited to the manna and their drink to the water that came out of the rock. Yet God preserved their health, so that they might know that He alone is the Giver of life and strength.

Moses returns to remind them of their victories over Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, and how they took possession of their lands, in which the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh settled. The credit for this was not theirs, but belonged to the Lord, who gave them this victory and helped them against their enemies.

Moses charges them to keep the words of the covenant and do them, and not to betray the covenant of the Lord which He made with them, so that they may prosper in their ways, that is, hold fast to God's commandments and His Law.
All the people stood to enter into the covenant with God, and it includes:
1- Your leaders: the seventy elders, the judges, the heads of the tribes, the captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and the heads of the clans.
2- Your tribes: the common people in all the tribes.
3- Your elders: the aged.
4- Your officers: the civil leaders.
5- The men of Israel: the adult males.
6- The little ones: those under twenty years of age.
7- Your wives: for the woman has a share in the blessings of the covenant just like the man.
8- Your strangers: prisoners of war or slaves from any other peoples, or those who joined them from other peoples.
For God wants to make His covenant with all the groups of the people, because He is a Father to all.

And just as God called the children in the Old Testament to enjoy the privileges of the covenant even though they did not understand, so also the Church of the New Testament grants her children the privileges of the covenant of grace, represented by the Holy Sacraments, such as the sacrament of Baptism, the sacrament of Confirmation, the sacrament of Holy Communion, and so on.

Here God renews His covenant with His people, which He had previously made with their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, so that they will be His people and be called by His name, and He will be a God to them who cares for them throughout their lives.

The covenant includes all the groups of the people with all their individuals, whether those present at the place or those absent for reasons of illness or old age, and not only the present generation but also the generations to come, that is, all believers, present and future.

God loves you and wants you to be a son to Him. You are not lost among the millions, but you have a place in the heart of God that no one else fills. So seize your opportunity, and pledge to live with Him and remain steadfast in His Church.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Moses brings back to the people's memory what they themselves witnessed during their stay in the land of Egypt, and during their passing through the midst of the other Gentile peoples after leaving Egypt on their way to the Promised Land, as they crossed various regions inhabited by pagan peoples, and the detestable customs and practices they saw, and the idols made by hands of wood, stone and metals.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Wormwood: a bitter plant.
Absinthe: a plant whose juice is extremely bitter and also poisonous.
Root: a person or a deviant group from which misleading speech results.

The Lord warns them lest any individual or group among them fall into the worship of idols, so that he or the group turns away from attachment to the Lord to worship the gods of the Gentiles. Then he becomes a cause of stumbling for others who follow his example, and causes the fall of many souls, so that he is like the intense bitterness that spreads bitterness in the mouths of many if they taste it.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Bless himself in his heart: justify himself.

This person, or the deviant group that brings evil upon itself and upon the rest of the people, when the curse which the Lord swore to bring upon those who betray His covenant is read in his hearing, takes no heed of the evils he commits, but rather approves of his deeds, insisting on acting according to his own desires, heedless of the Lord's warnings, saying to himself, "I shall be safe, even if I insist on continuing in this conduct of mine." This stubborn person works to spread evil among the people, so that the wrath of the Lord falls on all, the careless and the simple, whom this deviant person led astray and enticed to walk in evil.

What is meant by "to add drunkenness to thirst" is that the green and the dry perish alike. The one who is watered is he who has committed many iniquities to the full, as one who is watered has drunk his fill of water. The thirsty is he who abstains from iniquities but was enticed by the deed of the wicked person until it destroyed him, and he perished with him.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: The Lord will not spare this stubborn person who insists on worshiping idols, but will punish him with great wrath, like a fire that burns him so that smoke comes out of it, that is, God will destroy him and cast him into torment and the eternal fire. Thus the curses that are in the book of the covenant will fall upon him, and the Lord will destroy him and blot out his name from the earth.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Separate him unto evil: set him apart for evil.
The Lord sets him apart for all the plagues and woes that came in the curses mentioned in this book, so that misfortunes and afflictions fall upon him.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Your children in the generations to come, and the foreigners who come to your land from distant countries, will see what has befallen the land of Israel of plagues and diseases that the Lord allowed to come upon them, which are mentioned in the following verses.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Admah and Zeboiim: small towns surrounding Sodom and Gomorrah that were burned with them (Gen 14:

1, 2, Gen 19.(Destruction will strike all its land and it will become unfit for cultivation. The good land, which used to flow with milk and honey, will be covered with sulfur, salt and the remains of burning, exactly as happened to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: The other peoples, when they see the ruin that has befallen the land of Israel, ask in astonishment why the anger of the Lord was kindled against them to this great degree.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: The answer to this question will be that the reason for it is their betrayal of their covenant with the Lord the God of their fathers, the covenant which they made with Him after He brought them out of the land of their bondage, Egypt.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: And whom He had not given unto them: God did not permit them, but they are gods strange to them.

Their betrayal of the Lord consisted in their turning away from His worship and going to worship other gods strange to them and to their fathers, whom it was not for them to worship, for they are not their gods but the gods of pagan peoples and nations who do not know the true God as they have known and experienced Him.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: The Lord was greatly angered against them and brought upon them the curses that He had stated to them in a covenant before they entered the land of Canaan, which are mentioned in this book.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: Because of the intensity of the Lord's anger against them and His great displeasure at their conduct, He uprooted them from the Promised Land and emptied the holy land of them, because they had lost their worthiness of it by their turning away from Him, and He scattered them in other lands strange to them, so that they were dispersed and scattered throughout the world.
His words "as it is this day" mean the day on which the foreigners will see the ruin that has befallen the land.

entries.section: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

paragraphs.text: The secret things: the hidden wisdom of God, which human beings cannot understand however much their discoveries increase. Those things which are revealed: God's laws and teachings and all that He discloses to our minds.

Moses charges his people to hold fast to the commandments of God and His laws that are revealed to them, and not to be troubled because of the existence of divine mysteries they do not understand, since they will not be able to grasp all the wisdom of God with their limited minds.
Obey God's commandments and do not worry about the future or any obscure matters you do not understand, but only ask for His help and care, for He is your Father who guides you in all that you need.
The blessings of repentance and keeping the commandments

If you experienced the blessings of God when you obeyed His commandments, but afterward fell into sins and the curses came upon you, you can return to God by repentance, and He will forgive you and give you the blessings mentioned in the following verses (vv. 3-10). Thus the mercies of God are shown, who gives hope to His children however much they sin.

It is beneficial for a person, if he falls and misfortunes come upon him, to remember the blessings he used to enjoy when he was obedient to God, so that he may regain them by repentance, as the prodigal son did (Lk 15:17).
The outmost parts of heaven: the farthest places on earth, where, when a person looks toward them, he sees the sky as if it meets the earth.

The first blessing for the repentant people, whom the enemies enslaved, took captive and scattered in the lands of the world, is that God gathers them in His mercies and brings them back to their homeland, as happened in the return from captivity at the hands of Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah, because if the wicked person's heart returns to God by repentance, He restores to him his freedom and dignity.

God brings the people back to the land of their fathers and multiplies them more than they were in the days of their glory, for God's blessings to the repentant surpass every blessing, and this is the second blessing.

The third blessing is a person's return to the covenant with God, not only by the circumcision of the flesh but by the circumcision of the heart, that is, devoting it to the love of God. Circumcision in the Old Testament signifies Baptism, which is the renewal of man's nature to live with God (Col 2:11, 12).

The Lord turns the curses upon your enemies who drove you out of the land and oppressed you. Though the Lord had used them as a rod of discipline for His people, when the people repent God removes from them the yoke of those who enslaved them, and even afflicts them as they afflicted His people, so that the people of God are exalted and the enemies weakened. This is the fourth blessing.
The Lord accepts their repentance when they return and obey His voice, walk according to His statutes and judgments, and live a life of obedience, and this is the fifth blessing.

The Lord's blessings increase and He floods them with good things, so that they prosper in every work to which their hands reach, and He blesses their offspring, the produce of their cattle and their sheep, the crops of their land and the fruit of their trees. And when the Lord turns from His anger, He rejoices in their good and prosperity as He had rejoiced in the prosperity of their fathers when they were subject to His obedience and doing His commandments, and this is the sixth blessing.
The book of the Law: the book of Deuteronomy, which Moses was delivering to them.
The good things and blessings are conditional upon returning to God, repentance, and obeying the commandments mentioned in the book of the Law.

It is to be noted that when he spoke in the previous chapter about the punishment of the wicked, he mentioned God by the name "Jehovah the Lord," that is, God the Existing and the Just, whereas in this chapter he mentions Him by the name "the Lord your God," that is, your own God who loves you and gives you many blessings when you repent and return to Him.

Do not be distressed by the consequences of your sins and your repeated falling, but rise quickly, confident that the blessings of repentance are greater than you imagine, because God loves you and wants your salvation.

The commandment is not hard or burdensome, but it is within their ability to apply it in their lives as long as they are ready to receive it, for grace works and supports a person and helps him to obey the commandment.

The duties required of the people of Israel toward God are not fearsome, in a place difficult to reach. They are not in heaven, so that one must search for someone to go up there and bring them to them, nor do they require crossing seas and oceans to obtain them and bring them to them, to be read in their hearing so that they may do them. And if God in the Old Testament gave His people a clear and understandable commandment to carry out, then in the New Testament the commandment became clearer still through the Incarnation of Christ, who fulfilled the commandment and lived as an example for us.

The Lord brought His word to man, for it is He who drew near to him with it and put it in his mouth, to repeat it to himself and to teach it to others, and to keep it in his heart to meditate on it and do it, so that it may be his guide in all his ways. St. Paul quoted these verses in (Rom 10:5-10) to affirm the importance of trusting in God, believing His word and acting on it.
Take care to read the Holy Bible and meditate on it every day, so that you may apply it in your life and live in peace.

Understand well what I say to you. Man is given a choice between two ways: the way of good, which leads him to life, and the way of evil, which leads to death. For man is free in will and may choose between the two ways.
Life here is the joyful earthly life and also the blessed eternal life, and death is physical death and also spiritual death and eternal perdition.

The Lord gave His people all the commandments that are able to lead them to a blessed earthly and eternal life. These commandments are summed up in that he should love the Lord with all his heart, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments, statutes and judgments. By this he lives and grows in grace and bears fruit and enjoys the Lord's blessings in the land which he is entering to possess. And this is the summary of the Ten Commandments as Christ Himself declared (Lk 10:27).

And on the contrary, if you turn away from Me in your hearts and do not listen to My voice, but go astray and go after other gods besides the Lord your God to worship them, then without doubt your destruction is certain and you will perish. Likewise I assure you that you will be deprived of the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess, because the enemies will seize it and drive you out of it.

The Lord gives them His laws not in secret but openly before all, the heavenly and the earthly, and all living creatures bear witness that the Lord did not fall short in teaching them and warning them. And the Lord, in giving them a choice between the two ways in accordance with the principle of freedom given to man, nevertheless in His great love counsels them and urges them to choose life and blessing and to keep away from death and the curse.

The pillar of man's life is the love of the Lord, listening to His voice and attachment to Him, because God is the source of the life of all human beings, and He is our Creator, the origin of our existence and the Giver of all good things. And the Lord here promises them that their stay in the Promised Land will be long if they walk in His ways and obey His commandments.
You must choose the good yourself in order to obtain happiness on earth and in heaven, for happiness is within your reach if you seek it by cleaving to God and obeying His commandments.
The handing over of leadership to Joshua

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Moses began to speak to the people in a farewell address about the matters mentioned in the following verses up to (v. 6). He reminds the people that he has become an old man advanced in years, having reached one hundred and twenty, and that he is no longer able to lead the people as he did throughout the past forty years, from the time he worked to bring them out of Egypt until now. Moreover, the Lord had told him to transfer the leadership to another, for he would not cross the Jordan with his people into the Promised Land.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Moses reassures them that after his death the Lord will not leave them alone, for He will cross the river before them, represented by the ark of His covenant, which represents the presence of the Lord, and they will defeat the peoples who stand in their way. The Lord will destroy those peoples and give His people their land. Nor will the Lord leave them without a leader to lead them after his death, the death of Moses, for He had already appointed for them Joshua the son of Nun, the disciple of Moses, to lead them.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Just as the Lord gave them victory over Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, drove them out of their lands and gave their lands as a possession to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, He is able to do the same to the other peoples dwelling in the Promised Land, driving them out and giving His people possession in their place.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: When the victory over those peoples is achieved for them, they must deal with them as He had commanded them on more than one occasion, namely, that they destroy those peoples, tear down their altars and remove their traces, so that they would not afterward be influenced by their pagan worship.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Moses encourages them not to fear the might of the enemies, because God will walk in their midst and go before them, and will not forsake them or leave them alone to face the enemy.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Here Moses transfers the task of leading the people, as the Lord commanded him, to his disciple Joshua the son of Nun.

He calls him to take up the leadership before all the people, so that everyone may know that he is the new leader and that they must walk behind him. Moses urges him to be ready to bear the responsibility and to arm himself with courage, for he is the person charged by the Lord to enter with his people into the Promised Land, as He had promised their fathers to give them that land, and it is for him to divide the land among the tribes.

entries.section: (1) Moses' charge to the people and to Joshua

paragraphs.text: Moses reassures his disciple Joshua that he will not be alone in carrying out those tasks, for the Lord will lead him in his journey and accompany him in all his steps; He will take care of him and will not forsake him, so he should fear nothing and dread no enemy.
God chose Joshua to lead the people after Moses for the following reasons:
1- He was the special disciple who clung to Moses and learned from him more than all the others.
2- He went up alone with Moses on the mountain and remained forty days waiting for Moses until he returned with the commandments (Ex 24:13).
3- He and Caleb alone, out of all twelve spies, reassured the people and strengthened their faith to enter the Promised Land, but they refused (Num 14:6, 7).
4- He used to stand at the door of the tent of meeting when Moses left it, until he returned to it; this was the tent that preceded the tent that held the ark (Ex 33:11).
5- He led the war against Amalek and was victorious through the prayers of Moses.

If you receive a responsibility, do not be afraid, for God is with you. Ask for His help and go forward courageously toward the responsibility you are fulfilling, and He will complete His work in you.

entries.section: (2) The reading of the Torah at the Feast of Tabernacles

paragraphs.text: The Torah: a word meaning law, and it is the first five books of the books of the Old Testament, which Moses wrote under the guidance of the Lord. He completed it on that last occasion and then delivered it to the priests and the elders of the people, as those entrusted with keeping it, teaching it to the people and handing it down to the following generations. The priests are described as the bearers of the ark of the covenant because they were charged with the affairs of the ark, so they carried it, in place of the Kohathites (Num 4:6, 15) (the Levites of the clan of Kohath), on special occasions, such as what happened when the people crossed the Jordan behind the new leader Joshua the son of Nun (Josh 3:3).

entries.section: (2) The reading of the Torah at the Feast of Tabernacles

paragraphs.text: The Feast of Tabernacles: the third of the great principal feasts, in which the people must dwell in booths that they build in open places or on the roofs of houses, to remember their dwelling (they or their fathers) in tents throughout their journey in the wilderness of Sinai (Num 29:12-38). The year of release: every seventh year, also called the sabbath of the land because the land is not plowed in it. In it the creditor had to forgive his debt, and the Hebrew slave was set free. Moses commanded them to read this Law in the hearing of all the people when they gather in the year of release at the Feast of Tabernacles, in the place of the celebration, which is the holy place where the house of the Lord is established, such as Jerusalem (Lev 25:2).

entries.section: (2) The reading of the Torah at the Feast of Tabernacles

paragraphs.text: All the people, men and women, children and elders, Hebrews and resident strangers, had to come in the seventh year, the year of release, at the Feast of Tabernacles, to the place of the house of the Lord. The presence of the children here was by divine wisdom, that they might see the rites of the feast and hear the texts of the Law, so that this glorious picture would be fixed in their minds and remain engraved in their thoughts, and when they grew up and became men they would take over carrying them out and hand the tradition down to the following generations.

For this reason the Church of the New Testament is careful to urge fathers to bring their children, while they are still in childhood, to attend her blessed rites and to enjoy her Holy Sacraments, so that they grow up holding fast to her teachings and her doctrines take root in their souls.

entries.section: (2) The reading of the Torah at the Feast of Tabernacles

paragraphs.text: The sons of the following generations among them, who did not live through the Lord's glorious works with His people, hear the word of the Lord and learn from it His will and desire for their lives. So they live in His fear all the days that they remain in the land to which they are crossing the Jordan to settle in it.

Once again the Lord announces to Moses that his earthly life is about to end, and asks him to summon Joshua to the tent of meeting so that both of them may present themselves before the Lord, for the Lord often met with the people at the door of the tent of meeting, where He appeared in a pillar of cloud. So Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he and Joshua stood to receive what the Lord wanted to charge them with.

The glory of the Lord appeared in the pillar of cloud, which stood at the door of the tent. For God announces His presence among His people, the transfer of leadership from Moses to Joshua, and the encouragement of Joshua to carry out his new responsibility.
Break: betray the covenant.

The Lord announces to Moses anew that he will depart from the world and sleep as his fathers slept before him, having performed his mission in the best way. And the Lord declares to him, according to His foreknowledge of events, that the stubborn, fickle people will forsake their true God and betray His covenant with Him by going to worship gods strange to them, the gods of the peoples around them, after they dwell in the Promised Land.
Because my God is not in my midst...?: the people ask, could the cause of my misfortunes be that God has left me?

God's anger will be kindled against them in those days in which they will commit immorality, and He will leave them as they left Him and no longer look upon them with mercy, for they have lost their worthiness of His care and protection. Their enemies will humble them, and misfortunes and afflictions will come upon them until they repent, confess their sins, and know that what has befallen them is because the Lord has left them and no longer dwells in their midst because of their worship of idols.

Do not lose God's care for you and all His love for the sake of any passing desire or evil pleasure, for the love and care of God are more important than anything. And do not be lax about a small sin, lest it lead you to a greater one and God forsake you.

entries.section: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

paragraphs.text: The Lord commanded Moses to write a song whose details He would inspire him with, as it is recorded in the next chapter. He must teach it to the people, explain its details to them, and make them learn it so that it becomes fixed in their minds. The song contains comparisons between the Lord's great work with them and how they meet it with betrayal of His covenant.
Thus there are two means of strengthening the people's faith:
1- The Law of God.
2- The song that they repeat.
Praising God strengthens your faith in Him and increases your love for Him. So take care to praise God as part of your prayers at home and also in the Church.

entries.section: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

paragraphs.text: The Lord foretells to His people what will happen from them after they enter the Promised Land, which He promised their fathers and which overflows with many good things. Instead of thanking the Lord for His abundant kindnesses, which provided them with fullness and wealth, luxury and comfortable living make them forget the source of all good, who is God, abundant in mercies, so they break His covenant and worship other gods.

entries.section: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

paragraphs.text: When afflictions come upon the people and they repeat this song to which they are accustomed, they will remember that the cause of the afflictions is their distance from God. For God foretells them their coming evils so that they may guard against them and not do them.

entries.section: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

paragraphs.text: Moses obeyed the Lord's command to him, so he wrote the song and taught it to the children of Israel at the end of his life on earth, and it is what is written in (ch. 32).

entries.section: (4) A song to the Lord and the encouragement of Joshua

paragraphs.text: Then the Lord's charge to Joshua the son of Nun was to be strong in resolve and courageous in his leadership of his people to fight the enemies, assuring him that it is He who will lead His people and bring them into the Promised Land which He swore to their fathers to give them, and He also assured him that He will not leave him alone but will be with him and support him in his mission.

entries.section: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

paragraphs.text: When Moses finished writing the five books of the Torah, including the song mentioned, he commanded the priests of the tribe of Levi to take the copy of the Torah that he had written and put it beside the ark of the covenant, to declare the Lord's kindnesses to His people, His warnings to them, and the punishments awaiting them if they betray His covenant. They used to put it in a special chest beside the ark, in addition to other copies of the Torah that the priests kept to read to the people.

entries.section: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

paragraphs.text: For I have lived through the recklessness of your conduct toward the Lord and your repeated rebellion against Him. This happened despite my being among you and my attempt to teach you, guide you and care for you; how much worse will it be after my departure from this world?

entries.section: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

paragraphs.text: Your officers: the civil leaders.

Therefore he asked them to have all their elders gather to him, the heads of the tribes and the distinguished elite among them, so that he might recite to them the words of the song inspired to him by the Lord, that they might be responsible thereafter for instructing it and teaching it to the following generations of the people. And all living creatures, heavenly and earthly, and all of nature would be witnesses to the Lord's works with them and to their ingratitude and disobedience.

entries.section: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

paragraphs.text: For Moses knows what evils the people will commit in the future, as the Lord had already told him, and also from his previous experience with them. Therefore punishment comes upon them in the following generations.

entries.section: (5) The Torah beside the ark of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The congregation of Israel: includes the heads, the elders and the officers.

The elders gathered to him as the representatives and leaders of the people, and he recited in their hearing the words of the song in full, as a faithful teacher and trustworthy messenger who conveys faithfully what God wanted to say to His people.

Be committed to presenting God's word to all those around you, even if they will be affected by it only temporarily and may neglect it afterward, for perhaps you will win some of them, and your words will be a rebuke to the rest when they fall into sin and afflictions come upon them.
The song of Moses

Here Moses the prophet draws the attention of his hearers, the people of Israel, to the fact that the words they are about to hear are the word of the Lord, inspired to him to convey to his people. And these words are the song in which Moses calls heaven and earth, that is, all living creatures, to be witnesses against this people, to declare the justice of God in regard to the people's conduct if they violate the covenant.

A figurative description of the teachings of the Lord that Moses conveyed to the people, which are described as follows: Drop as the rain: as the rain falls on the earth and waters its plants, the teachings of the Lord come down to His people and water their spirits and develop their spirituality.
And distil as the dew: as the dew refreshes nature, those teachings refresh souls.
As the small rain upon the tender herb: as the rain is a watering of the grass on which the cattle graze, the teaching of the Lord is a watering of souls.
And as the showers upon the grass: as the heavy rain gives life to the herbs and makes them grow, so the word of the Lord gives life to souls and waters hearts.
Moses the prophet says that when he utters the song, he is calling upon the name of the person of the Lord and proclaiming the greatness of His glory and the generosity of His kindnesses.

He likens the Lord to a rock as the firm foundation on which His people rest, and "his work is perfect" means that His works are perfect, without lack or defect. All His dealings with human beings are just, and He remains faithful to His covenant and wrongs no one. He is righteous and free from every error, and gives each one according to his deeds, whether by reward or punishment, without injustice.

Would that you praised God every day in your prayers and glorified Him for all His works. This gives you reassurance and joy, and even shows on your face, so that you are cheerful and make others glad.

entries.section: (2) A rebuke of the people for disobedience

paragraphs.text: He prophesies of the sin of the children of Israel against the Lord and the corruption they will commit before Him, so that they no longer deserve to be called the sons of God or His own because of their blemishes and the deficiencies of their deeds, for they are a crooked generation, greatly perverse and fickle.

entries.section: (2) A rebuke of the people for disobedience

paragraphs.text: In a tone of reproach Moses faults them for meeting the Lord's kindnesses to them with such ingratitude and corruption. By this they showed a lack of understanding and wisdom, whereas it would have been better for them to think of the rights of His fatherhood over them, for He is their Creator and it is He who formed them into a chosen people apart from the other peoples.
Remember God's kindnesses to you, so that you are ashamed of your sins and turn away from them, and try to draw near to good works as a return of thanks for God's love and care for you.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: Thy father: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, or their father according to the flesh.

Moses urges the people to turn their memory back to the past and remember what the Lord provided His people of care and kindness over many generations, from the calling of their father Abraham, then Isaac and Jacob. And the young among them, who did not live in the time of God's leading of them by the hand of Moses in bringing them out of Egypt and His care for them in the wilderness of Sinai, should ask their fathers and the elders of the people, who were children in Egypt and lived through those events, to tell them what happened before of God's care for them, so that they increase in faith and trust in the Lord.

This is what our Church does, for she often takes us back to the lives of the saints and the sayings of the Fathers so that we increase in knowledge of the history of our Church and our martyrs, and the children's knowledge of the lives of their fathers grows, so that their faith is strengthened and they remain firm in the pure and correct teaching. So take care to read the history of the Church and the lives of the saints, and ask their intercessions so that they may accompany you in your life and you live strong and reassured.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: The text here speaks of the Promised Land, in that God had placed in His eternal plan that this piece of earth would be the portion of the children of Israel. From the time humanity was scattered over the earth, there were borders for every region inhabited by one of the peoples, and this holy land was inhabited by the Canaanites before the iniquity of these peoples was full, so that the Lord took it from them and gave it to His people at the time appointed in His divine purpose. So this land was the portion allotted by God to His people from of old.

In his saying "he set the bounds of the people" according to the number of the children of Israel (the sons of Jacob), he means the Canaanite peoples who inhabited the land of Palestine before it was taken from them and given to the sons of Jacob. The number of those peoples was twelve, the same as the number of the sons of Jacob and the tribes of Israel (Gen 10:15-18).

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: The portion: the share.
The lot of his inheritance: the boundaries of the share, the boundaries of the inheritance, since in ancient times they used to measure the land with a cord of known length.

God's portion is His children, and the children's portion is the Lord. So the song says that the Lord's portion is His people (Ps 16:5), meaning that the people of Israel are a people special to the Lord among all the peoples who divided the earth among themselves and were scattered in various directions, since it is the people who knew the true God above all other peoples.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: He speaks of God's care for His people in the wilderness of Sinai, a land in which life is difficult for lack of water or food, so God shepherded them, preserved them, fed them and cared for them as one cares for the most important thing in his body, which is his eyes.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: His wings: the shoulder, and its muscles are among the strongest muscles of the body.

Here he likens God's care and tending of His people to what the eagle does for her young, for she flutters over them as a figure of her care for them, and spreads her wings to fly with them, carrying them on her shoulders to teach them to fly.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: Thus the Lord did with His people, for He led them and cared for them with no strange god sharing in it. He took them by the hand so that they passed over the mountains of Sinai on their way in the wilderness, and He gave them to eat of the fruits that they found on their way, and of the wild honey that they came upon in the desert, and of the oil that they took from the olive trees that grow in rocky places.

entries.section: (3) The Lord's work with His people

paragraphs.text: Then when they entered the Promised Land they enjoyed its abundant good things. There was butter and milk from the produce of their many cattle, and they ate their flesh and fat, and they possessed the lands of Bashan, of which Og was king (ch. 3), which are lands rich in rams and sheep because of the abundance of their pastures. Likewise the wheat from which the finest kinds of flour are made is from the produce of the fertile lands in which they live, and they used to make wine from the fruit of the vines that flourish in the lands of Canaan, and the Lord blessed it as He blessed all its agricultural crops.

Reflect on God's care for you throughout your past life, and you will find wonderful works you did not expect. So thank God for them, that your enjoyment of what is in your hand now may increase and God's blessings to you may grow.
Kicked: rejected.
Jeshurun: a name given to the people of Israel, meaning the beloved.

Here he likens Israel to an unruly animal that the shepherd tended with the best care and fed with the best food until it grew fat from much eating, and instead of obeying its shepherd, it rejected him. Instead of thanking God for the abundance of His kindnesses, Israel rejected grace and loved disobedience, and left the Lord who had made of it a distinguished people and enfolded it with His care and blessing, and its eyes were blinded to the truth that God is its refuge, who saved it in the past and saves it in the present and the future, and this is the utmost folly on the part of the people of God. These are prophecies of what the children of Israel will do, and he will continue them in the following verses.

The Lord is jealous for His glory and for His people who worship other gods alongside their worship of Him, gods whom their fathers did not know, for they are strange to them. And they angered the Lord by their betrayal of Him and of His covenant. The expression that God was jealous and angry are human figures that bring the spiritual meaning near to the mind, and never mean that God is moved as human beings are moved, but mean the Lord's displeasure with the deeds and conduct of His people.
Newly come up: new gods.

The people offered sacrifices to gods who are not God, gods newly known to them, whose works they had never experienced before, as they had experienced God's works with them, and whom their fathers did not heed but rather despised.

He returns to liken the Lord to a rock, that is, that He is almighty and unchanging. It is He who formed them into a people and brought them out into the light and made them a strong people, feared by the peoples around them. But sadly the people forgot that it was God who formed them into a great people and brought it into being out of nothing and made it a great nation after it had been a small, weak company.

Know that every sin you commit is rebellion against God, and it is never right to meet God's kindnesses by committing these sins. So repent quickly, for He is merciful and receives you, and you regain your sonship and your glories.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: Moses the prophet continues his prophecies and announces that the Lord's decision, based on what happened of the people's betrayal of His covenant, is to neglect them and not look upon them.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said, I will no more shepherd them or care what happens to them, but I will look at what will come upon them of afflictions as a result of their deeds. They are not firm in their faith but are unfaithful, treacherous children who have forgotten God's love for them.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: They have stirred up My anger by their worship of false gods, idols made by the hands of men, so I too will stir up their jealousy and wrath. And God has indeed allowed ignorant pagan nations to trouble and persecute them, such as the nation of the Babylonians. These foreign nations signify the faith of the Gentiles in Christ at the time when many of the Jews refused to believe in Him (Jn 1:11, 12).

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: Their evil works kindle the fire of divine wrath, which burns even to the depths of hell, as if it extends from the surface of the earth to reach the depth of hell, so that the land on which they live becomes as though it were part of hell because of the dread of the torments to which they will be subjected. And in its extension from the surface of the earth it comes upon the fields and their crops and destroys the mountains from their foundations above their heads.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: The Lord sets afflictions and woes upon them, and they attack them like many armies, and He also aims His blows at them so that misfortunes strike them.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: The poison of serpents of the earth: the venom of reptiles.

For since they are exhausted by intense hunger resulting from the ruin of the land, and wearied by the burning fever and deadly diseases that have struck them, and have no strength at all to resist, God sets upon them the wild beasts that devour them with their fangs, and the poisonous reptiles that sting them with their venom.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: Bereaves: makes mothers lose their children.
Chambers: plural of chamber, the private room of the bridegroom and his bride.

If they appear outside their homes, the armies of the enemies kill them, so that their mothers are bereaved, and if they hide inside the houses, they are in trembling and fear. All are subject to this, whether young man or young woman, nursing infant or aged man.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: God decided in His anger to scatter His people among the peoples of the world, as happened in the days of the Assyrian or Babylonian kingdom, until the name of His people almost disappeared among the peoples of the earth.

entries.section: (5) The divine punishment for their rebellion

paragraphs.text: Here too fear and provocation are figurative expressions, for God does not fear and is not provoked, but what is meant is His anticipation of what the enemies of the children of Israel will say, if the Lord actually decides to carry out His plan of destroying them and blotting out their memory, for the enemies would claim that they were the ones who did that by their own power, and not that what happened was by the Lord's permission and will, since He used them as an instrument of discipline for His people. So in keeping His holy name, God did not blot out His people completely but disciplined them severely, and then, when they repented, brought them back to their land, that is, returned them from captivity.

If God allows you a trial, examine yourself lest it be because of your sins, and know that your God is merciful and wants your repentance, not your destruction. So return to Him by repentance, and He will remove the afflictions from you and you will enjoy His blessings.

entries.section: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

paragraphs.text: He continues his prophecies in these verses and shows that the nation of Israel will become devoid of understanding and discernment, as their shameful conduct proves. They are lacking in insight because they do not think of the consequence of what they do.

entries.section: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

paragraphs.text: If they were wise they would think much before committing those evil deeds, and would compare their state while enjoying the promises of God if they choose the way of life with their falling into the woes of which the Lord warned them many times if they disobeyed Him.

entries.section: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

paragraphs.text: Just as he showed what weakness the people of God will reach when they forsake Him (ch. 28:1, 7, 15, 18), so here he affirms the same meaning, announcing that one soldier of the enemies' soldiers will chase a thousand of them, and two will put ten thousand to flight, which means that victory or defeat is not by the strength of armies but by the will and pleasure of the Lord and by what accomplishes His divine plan. A defeat like this cannot be understood except that God was angry with them and in His anger delivered them to their enemies because they did not keep His covenant.

entries.section: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

paragraphs.text: Our mighty God is not like the weak gods of the enemies, and this is what the enemies themselves admit, even if the enemies sit as judges in the comparison between our strength and theirs.

entries.section: (6) The Jewish nation devoid of understanding

paragraphs.text: Here, in an eloquent simile, he mentions the evil deeds of Israel for which God delivers them to their enemies, saying:
Their vine is of the vine of Sodom: the vine is a grapevine whose fruits are bad, like Sodom, which committed many evils.

And of the fields of Gomorrah: here he likens the badness of the deeds of the children of Israel (that is, the fruit of their works) to vineyards, that is, grapevines that give bad fruit, like the wicked deeds of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are grapes of poison, their clusters are bitter: their fruit is deadly poison and all their deeds are shameful deeds that make whoever contemplates them feel intense bitterness.

The subject of vineyards and grapes here reminds us of what is in (Isa 5:1, 2), which means that the vineyard the Lord planted (which is the people of Israel), from which the Lord expected good grapes, yielded bad grapes.
Their wine is the poison of serpents and the deadly venom of asps: asps is the plural of asp, which is a snake, and the poison of serpents means the venom of serpents.
These peoples offer deadly poison, like the venom of serpents and snakes, instead of good wine.

If you care to be a disciple of the word of God and the teachings of the Church, you gain wisdom, understanding and guidance in all your steps in life, and you keep away from the toil of the world around you, immersed in desires that lead it to destruction.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: God gathers the fruits of the evil deeds of the children of Israel and puts them in His treasuries until the proper time for punishment, when He repays them for their errors and takes vengeance on them.

Here God likens the sins of the children of Israel, and likewise of the other peoples, to what a person keeps and stores in his treasuries and seals up. And God forgives them if the person repents, and repays for them if the person persists in his evil.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: God is the Avenger of the wicked and repays them justly for what they have committed. The Lord may delay sending punishment to give an opportunity for repentance, but the punishment is near, for it is known and decreed in His divine plan. Let not the wicked think that the Lord's delay means that He has overlooked their evils; rather He is patient with the sinner, hoping that this forbearance will lead him to repentance, but God at the same time prepares the retribution and carries out the punishment at the proper time.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: And though the Lord judges His people if they sin, He has compassion on them and has mercy on them if they repent and return to Him, and when He sees that their strength has weakened from the severity and dread of the blows and chastisements that came upon them, which struck everyone and from which neither free nor slave was exempted.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: God mocks the false gods that His people followed and relied upon, saying, where are they now that they are in this condition, and why did they not hasten to protect them and help them? The children of Israel used to offer sacrifices to them and pour out drink offerings, imagining that they eat and drink, when they are nothing but idols.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: The Lord tells them that it is He who punished them and He alone is able to deliver them, and no one shares divinity with Him. He has all authority to give life and to put to death. If He crushed them because of their evils in fulfillment of justice, He is also the Merciful One, able to heal them and deliver them from the lowliness and crushing in which they are.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: Lifting the hand to heaven: a gesture that indicates an oath, or an announcement of the disclosure of divine truths to human beings.
God declares and affirms that He is the only God and lives forever, and is not like the false gods and idols that neither move nor feel.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: My glittering sword: the shining sword.
My hand take hold on judgment: I have set myself up for judgment.
I whet my sword: I have made my sword sharp and ready to kill.

When the Lord decides to take vengeance on the peoples who were excessive in their cruelty to His people when God used them as a rod of discipline, He pictures Himself as a horseman preparing to enter a battle, whetting His shining sword to bring those peoples to judgment, taking vengeance on them and repaying them for what they did to His people and for their gloating over them, and also punishing them for all their evils, for they hated the Lord and worshiped idols.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: Here are wonderful similes by which the Lord depicts His vengeance on His enemies. His arrows with which He will strike the enemy will shed much blood, so that these arrows become as if drunk from having drunk so much of their blood. And His sword devours the flesh of the enemies, so the sword is covered with the blood of the enemies who will be killed, in addition to others who will be taken captive. The sword of the Lord will also cut off the heads of the enemy commanders, boasting in their strength.

entries.section: (7) God alone is the Repayer and the Benefactor

paragraphs.text: Rejoice, O Gentiles, His people: St. Paul quoted it in (Rom 15:10) from the Septuagint, "Rejoice, O Gentiles, His people." This is a reference to the Gentiles being made partakers with the people of God in the salvation in Christ, and rejoicing in the fulfillment of this wonderful salvation, for it is a prophecy of the salvation in Christ and the entry of the Gentiles into the faith.

And taking the text in its direct meaning, the writer of the song here calls the nations of the world to rejoice and praise the God of Israel, who avenges the blood of His people, returns vengeance upon His enemies, and is merciful to His land and to His people.

God defends you if you obey His commandments and always return to Him by repentance. And even if He allows disciplines for you and wrongs from others, be confident that they are temporary and that He will give you victory and glorify you in the end.

Moses declared the words of this song to the people and repeated it before them many times, that they might repeat it after him and memorize its words and its melodies. And Joshua the son of Nun helped him in having the people memorize it, because he was the leader next after him.

Moses charged them to teach this song to their children and have them memorize it, because it alerts them to keep the Law of God and to worship Him. This song bears witness against whoever memorizes it of the necessity of following God and encourages him in that.

Moses told them that the words of this song are not merely a tune or idle talk, but are the core of their life, establishing them in the upright life and ensuring them stability in the new land, the land of Canaan, so that no enemy crowds them in it.

Take care to memorize the Psalms and repeat them, not only at the appointed time of prayer but throughout the day, for they guard your thoughts and guide you in your words and conduct, so that you always live pure before God.

entries.section: (9) Moses sees the land of Canaan but does not enter it

paragraphs.text: This mount Abarim, mount Nebo: Mount Nebo is one of the chain of the mountains of Abarim, and its highest peak is the top of Pisgah (ch. 3:27). This mountain lies in the land of Moab east of the Jordan, opposite the city of Jericho, which lies west of the river (Map 6, 8). With Moses' having the people memorize the song, his service came to an end, so God commanded him to go up to the highest peaks of mount Abarim to see the Promised Land that God had promised His people, and then die rejoicing at having completed his service and the fulfillment of God's promises.

entries.section: (9) Moses sees the land of Canaan but does not enter it

paragraphs.text: God announced to Moses that he would die on this mountain and that God would hide his body, lest the children of Israel worship it because of their great love for him. Thus ends the life of Moses, the chief of the prophets, and he dies like the rest of human beings and like his brother Aaron, who died and was buried on mount Hor (Num 20:28).

entries.section: (9) Moses sees the land of Canaan but does not enter it

paragraphs.text: So that Moses might remain humble before God until the end of his life, He reminded him that he had sinned when he and Aaron doubted God's word, for instead of commanding the rock at Meribah to bring forth water, he struck it twice (Num 20.) But Moses' being deprived of entering the Promised Land because of this sin is not a belittling of Moses' greatness; rather, it represents a stage in the leadership of the people, since he had reached an advanced age, so that after him his disciple Joshua would begin a new stage, namely, entering the Promised Land.

It is good for us to follow the example of Moses the prophet and accept willingly any divine discipline that our Lord allows for us, accepting it without complaint or rebellion, and entrust our lives to Him with faith and thanksgiving, knowing that His merciful, loving hand will have compassion on us and will enter our lives to bring us out of affliction into light, for all that happens in our lives is part of His comprehensive divine plan for us and the fulfillment of His will in our existence.
The blessing of Moses upon the children of Israel
